citation: Rab17, a novel small GTPase, is specific for epithelial cells and is induced during cell polarization. (PMID: 8486736)
summary: RAB17 is the first identified epithelial cell-specific small GTPase, with mRNA expression restricted to kidney, liver, and intestine but absent from non-epithelial organs and fibroblasts. Expression is induced upon mesenchymal-to-epithelial differentiation in the developing kidney. By immunofluorescence and immunoelectron microscopy, Rab17 localizes to the basolateral plasma membrane and apical tubules, suggesting a role in transcellular transport.

citation: Rab17 localizes to recycling endosomes and regulates receptor-mediated transcytosis in epithelial cells. (PMID: 9624171)
summary: In MDCK cells stably co-expressing wild-type or mutant Rab17 with the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor (pIgR), Rab17 was found on small vesicles and tubules in the apical region and was accessible to dimeric IgA internalized via pIgR. Overexpression of Rab17 impaired basolateral-to-apical transcytosis of dimeric IgA, providing biochemical and morphological evidence that Rab17 regulates transcellular traffic through apical recycling endosomes.

citation: Small GTPase Rab17 regulates dendritic morphogenesis and postsynaptic development of hippocampal neurons. (PMID: 22291024)
summary: In mouse hippocampal neurons, Rab17 localizes specifically to dendritic growth cones, shafts, filopodia, and mature spines but is largely absent from axons. shRNA-mediated knockdown of Rab17 reduced dendrite growth, branching, and dendritic spine number, likely due to impaired filopodia formation, establishing Rab17 as a regulator of dendrite-specific membrane trafficking and postsynaptic development.

citation: ERK2 drives tumour cell migration in three-dimensional microenvironments by suppressing expression of Rab17 and liprin-β2. (PMID: 22328529)
summary: ERK2 (MAPK1) silencing in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells upregulates RAB17 expression, and re-expression of ERK2 (but not ERK1) restores RAB17 suppression and invasive migration. Knockdown of Rab17 rescues the invasiveness of ERK2-depleted cells, indicating that ERK2 drives cancer cell invasion specifically by transcriptionally suppressing RAB17.

citation: ALS2, the small GTPase Rab17-interacting protein, regulates maturation and sorting of Rab17-associated endosomes. (PMID: 31959474)
summary: ALS2 physically interacts with Rab17 and acts downstream of the Rab17-GEF RABGEF1 to regulate maturation of Rab17-residing nascent endosomes into EEA1-positive early endosomes. Upon Rac1 activation, Rab17 and ALS2 are co-recruited to membrane ruffles and early endosomes; Rab17 primarily localizes to recycling endosomes in a Rab11-dependent manner and nascent Rab17 endosomes arise via clathrin-independent endocytosis.

citation: Rab17 mediates differential antigen sorting following efferocytosis and phagocytosis. (PMID: 28005073)
summary: Mass spectrometry and immunofluorescence in macrophages showed that efferosomes (but not phagosomes) recruit Rab17, which directs degraded apoptotic cell-derived materials through the recycling endosome pathway, bypassing the MHC class II loading compartment. This Rab17-mediated trafficking prevents antigen presentation of apoptotic cell antigens, explaining why efferocytosis is immunologically tolerogenic compared to phagocytosis.

citation: Rab17 inhibits the tumourigenic properties of hepatocellular carcinomas via the Erk pathway. (PMID: 25707355)
summary: Rab17 expression was significantly reduced in HCC tissues compared to non-tumor hepatic tissues (37.1% vs 64.6%; P=0.0068), correlating with larger tumor size, poor differentiation, and metastasis. Overexpression of Rab17 in HCC cell lines inhibited proliferation, migration, colony formation, and xenograft tumor growth in vivo, and these anti-tumor effects were rescued by EGF-mediated ERK pathway activation, indicating Rab17 acts as a tumor suppressor partly through the ERK pathway.

citation: Rab17-mediated recycling endosomes contribute to autophagosome formation in response to Group A Streptococcus invasion. (PMID: 25052408)
summary: Rab17 colocalizes with GAS-containing autophagosome-like vacuoles (GcAVs) and mediates membrane supply from recycling endosomes (marked by transferrin receptor) to GcAVs during antibacterial autophagy. Overexpression of Rab17 increased TfR-positive GcAV content, while dominant-negative Rab17 (N132I) and knockdown of the upstream activator Rabex-5 reduced GcAV formation efficiency, identifying Rab17 as a key regulator of recycling endosome-to-autophagosome membrane fusion.

citation: Single-cell RNA-seq and bulk-seq identify RAB17 as a potential regulator of angiogenesis by human dermal microvascular endothelial cells in diabetic foot ulcers. (PMID: 37605780)
summary: RAB17 expression was significantly reduced in HDMECs from diabetic foot ulcer patients compared to healthy controls, and was identified as a characteristic gene by LASSO regression from bulk-seq and scRNA-seq data. Overexpression of RAB17 in vitro and in vivo enhanced tube formation, HIF-1α and VEGF-A expression, and diabetic wound healing, partially through the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway.

citation: RAB17 promotes endometrial cancer progression by inhibiting TFRC-dependent ferroptosis. (PMID: 39242574)
summary: RAB17 is overexpressed in endometrial cancer tissues and promotes cancer cell survival by suppressing ferroptosis through ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of the transferrin receptor (TFRC). RAB17 expression is further upregulated under low-glucose conditions, and the RAB17-TFRC axis limits ferroptosis to promote EC progression in glucose-deprived tumor microenvironments, validated by in vitro, in vivo, and clinical data.

citation: Multiple splice variants of phosphodiesterase PDE4C cloned from human lung and testis (PMID: 9349724)
summary: Multiple splice variants of PDE4C were cloned from human fetal lung and testis libraries, revealing tissue-specific isoform expression. PDE4C-delta54 was found only in testis, while the 5'-extended PDE4C-791 was seen only in lung and a melanoma cell line. Baculovirus-expressed PDE4C-delta54 was enzymatically active and sensitive to PDE4-specific inhibitors, confirming cAMP hydrolysis function.

citation: Aberrant TCF21 upregulation in adenomyosis impairs endometrial decidualization by increasing PDE4C expression (PMID: 39326465)
summary: In human endometrial stromal cells (HESCs), TCF21 overexpression directly increased PDE4C expression (confirmed by ChIP-seq/qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assay), which reduced intracellular cAMP levels and suppressed FOXO1 expression, thereby impairing decidualization. This TCF21/PDE4C/cAMP-FOXO1 axis was identified as a key mechanism underlying decidualization failure in adenomyosis patients.

citation: Integrated analysis using methylation and gene expression microarrays reveals PDE4C as a prognostic biomarker in human glioma (PMID: 24842301)
sample_size: 124 patient samples (56 low-grade, 63 high-grade glioma, 5 normal brain)
summary: PDE4C was found to be hypermethylated and downregulated in high-grade glioma; demethylation with 5-Aza-2'-deoxycytidine restored PDE4C expression in glioma cell lines. PDE4C siRNA knockdown reduced wild-type p53 expression, and overexpression in U87 cells promoted apoptosis and inhibited migration, supporting a tumor suppressor role via the p53 pathway.

citation: Hypoxia-conditioned BMSC exosomes improve short-term spinal cord injury outcomes via the miR-615-3p/PDE4C-mediated cAMP/PKA pathway (PMID: 41526970)
summary: miR-615-3p, enriched in hypoxia-conditioned BMSC-derived exosomes, directly targeted and suppressed PDE4C expression in spinal neurons, thereby activating the cAMP/PKA pathway. This reduced mitochondrial calcium overload and endoplasmic reticulum stress, and in a mouse SCI model, downregulation of PDE4C correlated with improved locomotor recovery and reduced tissue damage.

citation: Analysis of the effects of M2 macrophage-derived PDE4C on the prognosis, metastasis and immunotherapy benefit of osteosarcoma (PMID: 38774995)
summary: PDE4C was identified as a mediator between M2 macrophages and osteosarcoma (OS) cells via scRNA-seq; M2 macrophages transfer PDE4C mRNA to OS cells through exosomes. Elevated PDE4C in OS cells increased proliferation and mobility by upregulating collagen expression, and high PDE4C correlated with poor prognosis and reduced immunotherapy response.

citation: HNF4α-Mediated LINC02560 Promotes Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the miR-505-5p/PDE4C Axis (PMID: 40427523)
summary: LINC02560 acts as a competitive endogenous RNA by sponging miR-505-5p, thereby relieving suppression of PDE4C and leading to activation of P-AKT and EMT signaling pathways in papillary thyroid carcinoma cells. Silencing LINC02560 reduced PDE4C levels and inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion of KTC-1 and BCPAP cell lines.

citation: Elevated PDE4C level serves as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and correlates with poor survival in thyroid carcinoma (PMID: 38514754)
summary: Unlike PDE4A, PDE4B, and PDE4D which are downregulated in thyroid carcinoma (THCA), PDE4C expression was significantly upregulated across cancer stages, and higher PDE4C expression correlated with shorter progression-free survival. PDE4C was found to participate in cAMP metabolic processes by regulating adenylate cyclases (ADCY1, ADCY5, ADCY6, ADCY8, ADCY9) and was not enriched in the cAMP binding signal pathway unlike other PDE4 subtypes.

citation: Studying mechanisms of cAMP and cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase signaling in Leydig cell function with phosphoproteomics (PMID: 26643407)
summary: PDE4B and PDE4C, along with PDE8A and PDE8B, were found to be expressed in rodent Leydig cells. Combined inhibition of PDE4 and PDE8 dramatically increased steroid biosynthesis, and phosphoproteomic analysis in MA10 Leydig cells revealed that PDE4 inhibition (rolipram) regulated phosphorylation of proteins involved in cell cycle, lipid/glucose metabolism, transcription, and vesicle transport.

citation: Differential Expression of Inflammation-Related Genes in Children with Down Syndrome (PMID: 27293319)
sample_size: Children with Down Syndrome vs. controls
summary: PDE4C was among 12 inflammation-related genes found to be overexpressed in peripheral blood of children with Down Syndrome compared to controls, as measured by TaqMan qPCR array. This suggests PDE4C may contribute to the altered inflammatory responses observed in Down Syndrome, though it did not remain significant after FDR correction.

citation: PDE4C stabilized by ELAVL1 promotes lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer (PMID: 41868681)
summary: ELAVL1 (an RNA-binding protein) was shown to interact with PDE4C mRNA and increase its stability, confirmed by RNA pull-down and RNA immunoprecipitation assays. Silencing PDE4C or ELAVL1 suppressed BCPAP and TPC-1 cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and lymph node metastasis in vivo, establishing ELAVL1-mediated PDE4C stabilization as a driver of PTC metastasis.

variant_detail: Rare heterozygous variant in ATP2B4 (specific notation not provided in abstract)
phenotype: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)
diagnostic_reason: Rare heterozygous variant predicted damaging by multiple in silico prediction software; identified by whole exome sequencing; shared haplotype on chromosome 1 in affected individuals; proposed digenic inheritance with HSPG2 variant; incomplete penetrance noted (asymptomatic mother also carries variants)

phenotype: ATP2B4 expression upregulated in MPC-Exo-treated Mdx hearts (not a KO of ATP2B4 itself, but ATP2B4 identified as differentially expressed gene in Mdx mouse hearts)

phenotype: PMCA4b (ATP2B4) expressed in murine acinar cells; Pharmacological inhibition of PMCA4b worsened pancreatitis-induced injury; Pharmacological inhibition of PMCA4b blocked protective effects of recombinant renalase; No direct genetic knockout of ATP2B4 reported; inhibitor used as surrogate

citation: An erythroid-specific ATP2B4 enhancer mediates red blood cell hydration and malaria susceptibility. (PMID: 28714864)
summary: eQTL mapping in erythroblasts identified erythroid-specific regulatory SNPs for ATP2B4, the main calcium ATPase of red blood cells, previously associated with mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) and severe malaria susceptibility. Atp2b4-/- mice showed increased MCHC, confirming ATP2B4 as the causal gene. CRISPR-Cas9 fine-mapping identified an erythroid-specific enhancer whose deletion caused abnormally high intracellular calcium levels in erythroid cells.

citation: Identification of ATP2B4 Regulatory Element Containing Functional Genetic Variants Associated with Severe Malaria. (PMID: 35563239)
summary: Five ATP2B4 SNPs in linkage disequilibrium with the malaria-associated variant rs10900585 were identified in a regulatory region and shown to have significant associations with severe malaria in a Senegalese population. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of this regulatory region decreased ATP2B4 transcript and protein levels and increased intracellular Ca2+ concentration in K562 cells. These results demonstrate that severe malaria-associated variants alter ATP2B4 expression, likely affecting malaria risk through calcium concentration effects on parasitaemia.

citation: Genetic variations in human ATP2B4 gene alter Plasmodium falciparum in vitro growth in RBCs from Gambian adults. (PMID: 36604655)
significance: p<0.0001 for protein expression and calcium expulsion; p<0.01 for parasite growth
summary: RBCs from homozygous carriers of the minor allele of ATP2B4 tagging SNP rs1541252 showed significantly reduced PMCA4b protein expression and slower rates of calcium expulsion compared to heterozygotes and wildtypes. Growth of P. falciparum laboratory and field isolates was significantly decreased in RBCs from homozygotes, and parasite growth was inhibited by the PMCA4b inhibitor aurintricarboxylic acid. These findings support the hypothesis that this ATP2B4 genotype protects against severe malaria by suppressing parasitaemia through altered calcium dynamics.

citation: The calcium pump PMCA4b promotes epithelial cell polarization and lumen formation. (PMID: 40075218)
summary: PMCA4 (ATP2B4) is downregulated in luminal breast cancer and its reduced expression is associated with shorter relapse-free survival in luminal A and B1 subtype tumors. In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, PMCA4 silencing caused loss of cell polarity while forced PMCA4b overexpression induced cell polarization and lumen formation. Silencing of the single pmca gene in Drosophila melanogaster larval salivary gland destroyed lumen morphology, suggesting a conserved role of PMCAs in lumen morphogenesis.

citation: Genetic Screening of Haploid Neural Stem Cells Reveals that Nfkbia and Atp2b4 are Key Regulators of Oxidative Stress in Neural Precursors. (PMID: 38666459)
summary: A high-throughput genetic screen in mouse haploid neural stem cells (haNSCs) identified Atp2b4 as significantly upregulated in Nfkbia-null NSCs, which show resistance to H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Overexpression of Atp2b4 itself increased survival of NSCs in the presence of H2O2, demonstrating that Atp2b4 is a key regulator of oxidative stress resistance in neural precursors. This identifies a novel role for ATP2B4 in neuroprotection against reactive oxygen species.

citation: ATP2B4 is an essential gene for epidermal growth factor-induced macropinocytosis in A431 cells. (PMID: 38597132)
summary: Knockout of ATP2B4 in A431 human epidermoid carcinoma cells inhibited ruffle closure and macropinosome formation during EGF-induced macropinocytosis without affecting ruffle formation. ATP2B4-KO also reduced EGF-stimulated Ca2+ oscillation during macropinocytosis, and the effect required PMCA4 pump activity independent of its PDZ domain-binding motif. These findings establish ATP2B4 as an essential regulator of Ca2+ dynamics required for EGF-induced macropinocytosis.

citation: A microRNA-129-5p/Rbfox crosstalk coordinates homeostatic downscaling of excitatory synapses. (PMID: 28487411)
summary: Atp2b4 was identified as a direct target of miR-129-5p in hippocampal neurons during synaptic downscaling induced by picrotoxin treatment. Restoring Atp2b4 expression was sufficient to prevent synaptic downscaling in PTX-treated neurons, and the RNA-binding protein Rbfox1 normally promotes Atp2b4 expression but is downregulated by miR-129-5p upon elevated network activity. This identifies Atp2b4 as a key effector in activity-dependent homeostatic synaptic plasticity with implications for epileptogenesis.

citation: Circadian miR-449c-5p regulates uterine Ca(2+) transport during eggshell calcification in chickens. (PMID: 34702171)
summary: ATP2B4 mRNA and protein were rhythmically expressed in the chicken uterus and confirmed as a direct target of circadian miR-449c-5p by dual-luciferase reporter assays. Overexpression of ATP2B4 significantly decreased intracellular Ca2+ concentration while knockdown accelerated intracellular Ca2+ accumulation in uterine tubular gland cells. These results demonstrate that ATP2B4 promotes uterine Ca2+ trans-epithelial transport and is regulated by clock-controlled miR-449c-5p during eggshell calcification.

citation: Molecular and Electrophysiological Analyses of ATP2B4 Gene Variants in Bilateral Adrenal Hyperaldosteronism. (PMID: 32002807)
summary: Rare ATP2B4 variants were identified in patients with bilateral hyperaldosteronism (BHA), and endogenous ATP2B4 expression was characterized in adrenal tissue. Whole-cell recordings in HAC15 adrenal cells revealed robust endogenous ATP2B4 conductance, and knockdown of ATP2B4 reduced angiotensin II stimulation in one of four shRNA clones. However, ATP2B4 variants did not significantly alter basal or agonist-stimulated CYP11B2 (aldosterone synthase) expression, and a pathogenic role for ATP2B4 variants in BHA was not confirmed.

citation: Altered ion-responsive gene expression in Mmp20 null mice. (PMID: 20929715)
summary: Expression of Atp2b4 was significantly decreased in enamel organs from Mmp20-/- mice compared to wild-type, alongside other ion-regulatory genes (Slc4a2, Car6, Cftr). This reduction was associated with attenuated pH changes during enamel development in null mice, suggesting Atp2b4 participates in ion regulation during enamel maturation. The findings indicate a feedback mechanism regulates ion-responsive gene expression, including Atp2b4, during enamel development.

citation: SARS-CoV-2-Induced PAPOLG Contributes to Inflammation Response by Stabilizing NF-κB mRNA. (PMID: 40607946)
summary: PAPOLG was significantly upregulated in SARS-CoV-2-infected THP-1 macrophages. Knockdown of PAPOLG promoted NF-κB mRNA degradation and decreased TNF-α and IL-6 levels, while overexpression of PAPOLG stabilized NF-κB mRNA and enhanced cytokine expression. These results demonstrate that PAPOLG contributes to inflammatory responses by stabilizing NF-κB mRNA via alternative polyadenylation.

citation: Systematic analysis of the frequently amplified 2p15-p16.1 locus reveals PAPOLG as a potential proto-oncogene in follicular and transformed follicular lymphoma. (PMID: 31410080)
summary: Amplification of the 2p15-p16.1 locus is associated with increased transcription of PAPOLG in transformed follicular lymphoma (tFL), and PAPOLG expression increases after histological transformation from FL to tFL. Compared with normal B-cells, PAPOLG was significantly overexpressed in FL cases, while other genes in the locus (BCL11A, PUS10, USP34) did not show significant differences. These findings suggest PAPOLG may be the most critical gene in the 2p15-p16.1 amplicon for lymphoma transformation.

citation: Comprehensive analysis of GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG axis in hepatocellular carcinoma. (PMID: 35482720)
summary: Bioinformatics analysis identified PAPOLG as a component of the ceRNA network axis GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG in hepatocellular carcinoma, where PAPOLG is highly expressed and associated with poor prognosis. Immune infiltration analysis suggested this axis may affect macrophage polarization. A risk-prognosis model incorporating this axis predicted patient survival with AUC values of 0.691, 0.623, and 0.626 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively.

citation: A diet rich in high-glucoraphanin broccoli interacts with genotype to reduce discordance in plasma metabolite profiles by modulating mitochondrial function. (PMID: 23964055)
sample_size: subjects in HG broccoli arm of a 12-week dietary intervention
summary: SNPs associated with the PAPOLG gene were found to differentiate two discrete phenotypic responses to a high-glucoraphanin broccoli dietary intervention in a randomized controlled trial. PAPOLG genotype significantly affected plasma metabolic profiles including lipid and amino acid metabolites, TCA cycle intermediates, and acylcarnitines (p<0.001), and a significant PAPOLG genotype × diet interaction was observed (p<0.001). The HG broccoli diet reduced metabolic variation between the two PAPOLG genotype groups, consistent with rebalancing of mitochondrial metabolic reactions.

citation: A combined blood based gene expression and plasma protein abundance signature for diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer--a study of the OVCAD consortium. (PMID: 23551967)
sample_size: 343 samples (90 healthy, 6 cystadenoma, 8 low malignant potential tumor, 19 FIGO I/II, 220 FIGO III/IV EOC patients); validation: 65 controls and 224 EOC patients
summary: PAPOLG was identified as one of 13 genes differentially expressed in leukocytes from epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) patients compared to controls. PAPOLG expression was included in a combined diagnostic model using gene expression and plasma protein biomarkers that achieved an AUC of 0.998 and a bootstrap-validated classification error of 2.8–3.1% for discriminating EOC patients from controls. This indicates PAPOLG is part of an immune response gene expression signature detectable in blood that is associated with EOC.

citation: Oocyte quality and in vivo embryo survival after ovarian stimulation in nulliparous and multiparous rabbit does. (PMID: 35724452)
summary: PAPOL-G (PAPOLG) gene expression in rabbit oocytes was significantly different among experimental groups (nulliparous vs. multiparous, superovulated vs. control), indicating that both hyperstimulation treatment and reproductive history alter PAPOLG transcription in oocytes. PAPOLG was among only 4 of 11 analyzed genes (along with MATER, PAPOL-A, and ZAR-1) showing differential expression, suggesting a specific role in oocyte maturation and competence acquisition. These findings link PAPOLG expression to oocyte quality and in vivo embryo viability.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Refining the 2p15-p16 Microdeletion Syndrome. (R. Lozano, W. Wilcox)
sample_size: 1 patient (sixth reported case of 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome)
summary: PAPOLG is located within the 2p15-p16.1 microdeletion region associated with a syndrome characterized by developmental delay, microcephaly, and dysmorphic features. In a patient with a 1.11 Mb deletion at 2p15-16.1, PAPOLG was among the deleted genes, though the critical region for the neurodevelopmental phenotype was refined to exclude PAPOLG and implicate other genes such as KIAA1841. This report contextualizes PAPOLG's genomic location but does not assign it a causative role in the syndrome.

citation: Analysis of differentially expressed microRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid. (PMID: 35997417)
summary: PAPOLG was identified as a predicted target gene of differentially expressed miRNAs (including bta-miR-196a, bta-miR-2285aj-5p, bta-miR-143, bta-miR-2433, bta-miR-2284f, and bta-miR-2368-3p) in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid to model Staphylococcus aureus-induced mastitis. Target gene enrichment analysis placed PAPOLG and co-targets in the MAPK signaling pathway, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer pathways. This suggests PAPOLG may be regulated by miRNAs during inflammatory responses in mammary epithelial cells.

citation: N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea-Induced Adaptor Protein 2 Sigma Subunit 1 (Ap2s1) Mutations Establish Ap2s1 Loss-of-Function Mice (PMID: 29479578)
summary: AP2S1 encodes the AP2σ subunit of the heterotetrameric AP-2 complex (with AP2α, AP2β, and AP2μ), which is pivotal for clathrin-mediated endocytosis. citation: The HAVCR1-centric host factor network drives Zika virus vertical transmission (PMID: 40156834)

citation: Proteomics Reveals AP-2 Complex Depletion Suppressing Listeria monocytogenes Intracellular Replication (PMID: 40847839)

CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of Ap2s1 (along with Ap2m1 and Ap2a2) markedly inhibited intracellular bacterial proliferation. These findings establish AP2S1 as a host factor exploited by L. monocytogenes to promote post-phagosomal cytosolic replication.

citation: GTPase GPN3 facilitates cell proliferation and migration in non-small cell lung cancer by impeding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of EGFR (PMID: 39893205)

citation: Codon Arg15 mutations of the AP2S1 gene: common occurrence in familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia cases negative for calcium-sensing receptor (CASR) mutations (PMID: 24731014)
summary: Recurrent missense mutations at codon Arg15 of AP2S1 (p.R15C, p.R15L, p.R15H) were identified in 5 of 39 (13%) FHH patients lacking CASR mutations, confirming AP2S1 as a cause of FHH type 3. AP2S1 encodes a sigma subunit that interacts with the CaSR and is required for its proper internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. The FHH3 phenotype did not differ materially from FHH1 caused by CASR mutations.

citation: In Vitro Control of Genes Critical for Parathyroid Embryogenesis by Extracellular Calcium (PMID: 32666007)
summary: AP2S1 mRNA expression was assessed in primary cultures of adult parathyroid adenoma tissue under varying extracellular calcium concentrations (0.1–3.0 mM). Unlike CaSR and GNA11, which showed sensitivity to low calcium concentrations, AP2S1 exhibited a variable and less pronounced response to extracellular calcium. This study places AP2S1 within the calcium regulatory signaling pathway expressed in adult parathyroid cells.

citation: Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia Types 1 and 3 and Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Similarities and Differences (PMID: 26963950)
sample_size: 22 FHH type 3 patients, 52 FHH type 1 patients, 60 PHPT patients
summary: In a large cohort, three recurrent AP2S1 mutations were identified in 19 families with FHH type 3, establishing AP2S1 loss-of-function as a distinct genetic cause of FHH. Patients with FHH type 3 (AP2S1 mutations) had higher plasma calcium concentrations and higher renal tubular calcium reabsorption than FHH type 1 (CASR mutations), despite similar PTH levels. This indicates that AP2S1 mutations affect calcium homeostasis more severely than CASR mutations.

citation: Proteomic analysis of boar sperm with differential ability of liquid preservation at 17 °C (PMID: 38029685)
summary: Quantitative proteomics (TMT labeling) of boar sperm identified AP2S1 as one of 8 candidate biomarker proteins differentially expressed between sperm with good versus poor liquid preservation ability. AP2S1 was identified through protein-protein interaction network analysis as a hub protein among 187 differentially expressed proteins. This suggests AP2S1 protein is present and functionally relevant in boar sperm.

citation: Analysis of AP2S1, a calcium-sensing receptor regulator, in familial and sporadic isolated hypoparathyroidism (PMID: 24423332)
summary: Sequencing and quantitative genomic PCR of AP2S1 in 60 patients (10 familial, 50 sporadic) with isolated hypoparathyroidism found no nucleotide changes or copy number variations, excluding AP2S1 defects as a frequent cause of hypoparathyroidism. This study characterizes AP2S1 as a calcium-sensing receptor regulator whose gain-of-function (not loss-of-function) is associated with hypercalcemic rather than hypocalcemic phenotypes. The negative result clarifies the directional specificity of AP2S1 mutations in calcium disorders.

citation: ADCY5 gene expression in adipose tissue is related to obesity in men and mice (PMID: 25793868)
summary: Visceral ADCY5 mRNA expression is significantly higher in obese compared to lean individuals and correlates with BMI, body fat mass, circulating leptin, fat distribution, and waist/hip circumference, but not with fasting plasma glucose or HbA1c. In mice, adipose tissue Adcy5 expression is significantly higher after a high-fat diet compared to standard chow.

citation: Effects of theophylline on ADCY5 activation-From cellular studies to improved therapeutic options for ADCY5-related dyskinesia patients (PMID: 36867608)
summary: In ADCY5-overexpressing cell lines, caffeine, theophylline, and istradefylline all reduced ADCY5-catalyzed cAMP production, with the most pronounced effects observed for the gain-of-function R418W mutant. The R418W mutant exhibits increased catalytic activity resulting in elevated cAMP levels, and theophylline treatment of a patient with this mutation produced striking clinical improvement in dyskinesia symptoms.

citation: ASHG 2015 - A functional regulatory variant associated with type 2 diabetes and fasting glucose levels at the ADCY5 locus (T. S. Roman et al.)
summary: The rs11708067-A risk allele at the ADCY5 locus overlaps FAIRE and DNase peaks and a strong enhancer chromatin state in human pancreatic islets, and shows lower enhancer activity in luciferase reporter assays in rat insulinoma cells compared to the G allele. RNA-seq from 114 islet samples confirmed decreased ADCY5 expression for the rs11708067-A allele, suggesting the risk allele decreases ADCY5 expression to raise fasting glucose and T2D risk.

citation: ADCY5 act as a putative tumor suppressor in glioblastoma: An integrated analysis (PMID: 39319137)
summary: ADCY5 mRNA and protein are downregulated in GBM compared to normal tissues, and its expression is negatively correlated with DNA methylation. Re-expression of ADCY5 in GBM cell lines inhibited cell proliferation, viability, migration/invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in vitro, supporting a tumor suppressor role.

citation: Artemisinin alleviates Parkinson's disease by targeting Adcy5-Gch1 axis to trigger a cascade generation of BH4 and dopamine in rats (PMID: 40908481)
summary: Molecular docking and in vivo/in vitro experiments demonstrated that artemisinin directly binds Adcy5 and increases Adcy5 and Gch1 (BH4 synthetase) expression, boosting BH4 and dopamine production. Inhibition of Adcy5 in vivo aggravated Parkinson's disease manifestations, decreased midbrain dopamine and BH4 production, and downregulated Gch1, establishing an Adcy5-Gch1-BH4 axis as a neuroprotective pathway.

citation: Loss of IRF2BPL impairs neuronal maintenance through excess Wnt signaling (PMID: 35044823)
summary: IRF2BPL and its Drosophila ortholog Pits repress Wnt transcription; neuronal depletion of Pits increases wingless (wg) levels in fly brains causing axonal loss, while inhibition of Wg signaling is neuroprotective. Loss of irf2bpl in zebrafish increases wnt1 transcription and downstream signaling, and WNT1 is elevated in patient-derived astrocytes. IRF2BPL physically and genetically interacts with the Wnt antagonist CKIα to antagonize Wnt transcription and signaling.

citation: Mechanisms of IRF2BPL-related disorders and identification of a potential therapeutic strategy (PMID: 36476864)
summary: Patient skin fibroblasts reprogrammed to astrocytes and neurons showed that truncated IRF2BPL variants sequester wild-type protein to the cytoplasm and cause aggregation, while full-length IRF2BPL localizes to the nucleus. Patient astrocytes failed to support neuronal survival in coculture and exhibited aberrant mitochondria and respiratory dysfunction. Treatment with CuATSM rescued neuronal survival and restored mitochondrial function in vitro.

citation: IRF2BPL Is Associated with Neurological Phenotypes (PMID: 30057031)
summary: The Drosophila IRF2BPL ortholog pits is broadly expressed including in the nervous system; complete loss of pits is lethal early in development, whereas partial RNAi knockdown in neurons leads to neurodegeneration. IRF2BPL nonsense variants behave as severe loss-of-function alleles in flies, while missense variants produce a range of phenotypes, demonstrating a requirement for this gene in neuronal function and maintenance.

citation: Forkhead Box F2 Suppresses Gastric Cancer through a Novel FOXF2-IRF2BPL-β-Catenin Signaling Axis (PMID: 29374064)
summary: FOXF2 directly binds the promoter of IRF2BPL and induces its transcriptional expression; IRF2BPL in turn interacts with β-catenin, increasing its ubiquitination and degradation independently of GSK-3β. This FOXF2-IRF2BPL axis suppresses Wnt signaling and acts as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer. IRF2BPL is thus identified as an E3 ligase that ubiquitinates β-catenin.

citation: IRF2BPL inhibits proliferation, migration and invasion of osteosarcoma cells by inhibiting FOSL2-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway activation (PMID: 40834975)
summary: IRF2BPL is downregulated in osteosarcoma and its overexpression suppresses cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro and in vivo, while silencing enhances these processes. Mechanistically, IRF2BPL regulates the FOSL2/PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis through ubiquitin-mediated degradation of FOSL2. A subcutaneous xenograft tumor model validated its tumor-suppressive role in vivo.

citation: IRF2BPL transcriptionally regulates IGFBP2 to promote tumor progression and suppresses immune cell infiltration in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 41413713)
summary: IRF2BPL acts as a transcriptional activator (non-classical E3 ubiquitin ligase function) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, promoting IGFBP2 transcription and facilitating malignant phenotypes both in vivo and in vitro. IRF2BPL is highly expressed in ESCC cells and its hyperactive IRF2BPL-IGFBP2 axis also inhibits immune cell infiltration in the tumor microenvironment. The chemical ONC201 effectively impeded ESCC progression driven by this axis.

citation: N(6)-methyladenosine-modified circRNA RERE modulates osteoarthritis by regulating β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 35733354)
summary: IRF2BPL functions downstream of the circRERE/miR-195-5p axis to regulate ubiquitination and degradation of β-catenin in chondrocytes, exerting chondroprotective effects in osteoarthritis. AAV-mediated knockdown of Irf2bpl in a mouse destabilization of medial meniscus model worsened OA severity, and these detrimental effects were counteracted by the β-catenin inhibitor ICG-001. This study confirms IRF2BPL's role as a regulator of β-catenin ubiquitination in a non-neurological tissue context.

citation: IRF2BPL-Related Disorder, Causing Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Regression, Abnormal Movements, Loss of Speech and Seizures (NEDAMSS) Is Characterized by Pathology Consistent with DRPLA (PMID: 39224955)
summary: Postmortem pathological analysis of an IRF2BPL-related disorder patient revealed findings consistent with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including polyglutamine (polyQ) inclusions, suggesting a novel disease mechanism involving the polyQ repeat tract. The IRF2BPL c.562C>T variant resulted in decreased mRNA in brain tissue and destabilization of the protein product with downstream molecular abnormalities in patient-derived cells. This is the first detailed pathological description of NEDAMSS.

citation: Neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a truncating de novo variant of IRF2BPL (PMID: 33278788)
summary: In cells harboring a truncating IRF2BPL mutation, the cellular localization of IRF2BPL was altered and the level of ubiquitinated proteins was significantly decreased compared to control cells, implicating impairment of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. Bioinformatics predicted IRF2BPL association with IRF2 and 10 other genes involved in ubiquitin binding pathways. These findings support a role for IRF2BPL in ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation relevant to neurological disease.

citation: Differential Retinal Protein Expression in Primary and Secondary Retinal Ganglion Cell Degeneration Identified by Integrated SWATH and Target-Based Proteomics (PMID: 34445296)
summary: IRF2BPL was identified as one of six proteins regulated in both temporal and nasal retinal quadrants following localized optic nerve injury in adult Wistar rats, suggesting a role in retinal ganglion cell degeneration. Proteomic analysis using SWATH-MS and MRM-MS detected IRF2BPL expression changes in the context of primary and secondary RGC degeneration. This provides evidence for IRF2BPL expression and regulation in the retina under neurodegenerative conditions.

summary: Using electrically switchable DNA biochips and single-molecule mass analysis, the leucine zipper (LZ) domain of FOXP2 was found to mediate dimerization via coiled-coil formation and also contributes to DNA binding. The zinc finger (ZF) domain contributes to dimerization when the LZ coiled-coil is intact but is not involved in DNA binding, while the forkhead domain (FHD) is the key driver of DNA binding.

citation: DNA binding and mitotic phosphorylation protect polyglutamine proteins from assembly formation (PMID: 40239647)
summary: FOXP2 contains a long polyglutamine tract but avoids pathogenic aggregation through two mechanisms: DNA binding during interphase has a solubilizing effect, and multiple phosphorylation events during mitosis promote chromatin eviction and maintain solubility. Human-specific amino acid substitutions linked to speech evolution map to a mitotic phospho-patch ('EVO patch') that reduces the propensity of human FOXP2 to assemble.

summary: In human pluripotent stem cell-derived thalamic organoids, the 22q11.2 microdeletion causes elevated FOXP2 expression in thalamic neurons and glia. Using an organoid co-culture model, FOXP2 overexpression was shown to mediate thalamic axon overgrowth in a FOXP2-dependent manner, with ROBO2 identified as a candidate downstream mediator of this effect.

citation: Tubular FoxP2 and Kidney Fibrosis (PMID: 39656554)
summary: FOXP2 is upregulated in kidney tubular cells via TGF-β/Smad3 signaling and promotes kidney fibrosis by activating epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and G2/M cell cycle arrest. ChIP-seq identified FOXP2 target genes enriched in PI3K/AKT and TGF-β signaling pathways, with direct transcriptional regulation of collagen-1, E-cadherin, and p21. Tubule-specific Foxp2 knockout mice showed attenuated fibrosis in UUO and UIRI models.

citation: Molecular and cellular evolution of the primate dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (PMID: 36007006)
summary: Single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis of over 600,000 nuclei from human, chimpanzee, macaque, and marmoset dlPFC revealed that FOXP2 expression in microglia is human-specific, while its expression in layer 4 granular neurons is primate-specific. This represents a species-specific molecular difference in a neuropsychiatric risk gene across anthropoid primates.

citation: FOXP genes regulate Purkinje cell diversity and cerebellar morphogenesis (PMID: 40826298)
summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of the embryonic mouse cerebellum identified at least 11 molecularly distinct Purkinje cell subtypes whose identity is defined by combinatorial expression of Foxp1, Foxp2, and Foxp4. Genetic deletion of Foxp1 and Foxp2 disrupts Purkinje cell diversification and cerebellar patterning, including failure of cerebellar hemisphere formation.

citation: Foxp2 Regulates Identities and Projection Patterns of Thalamic Nuclei During Development (PMID: 27384060)
summary: Foxp2 shows a graded expression pattern in the mouse thalamic primordium (high posterior, low anterior). In Foxp2(R552H) knockin mice carrying a loss-of-function missense mutation in the forkhead domain, posterior thalamic nuclei were shrunken while intermediate-region nuclei expanded, and thalamocortical projection patterns were altered, demonstrating a role for Foxp2 in thalamic patterning and connectivity.

citation: FOXP2/SOS1/AKT negative feedback loop inhibits cell proliferation in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer (PMID: 40813540)
summary: FOXP2 is significantly downregulated in colorectal cancer tissues and its high expression correlates with favorable prognosis in KRAS-mutant patients. Mechanistically, FOXP2 transcriptionally represses SOS1, thereby attenuating downstream PI3K/AKT signaling and inducing G0/G1-phase arrest; AKT activation in turn enhances FOXP2 expression, forming a negative feedback loop. These findings were validated in KRAS-mutant CRC cell lines and in vivo xenograft models.

citation: Structural architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 34929720)
summary: Cryo-EM structure of the ~1-MDa NALCN channelosome reveals that UNC79 and UNC80 are massive HEAT-repeat proteins forming an intertwined anti-parallel superhelical assembly that docks intracellularly onto the NALCN-FAM155A pore-forming subcomplex. Calmodulin copurifies bound to the C-terminal domain of NALCN, identifying it as a putative modulatory hub. Single-channel analyses uncovered a low open probability for the wild-type complex, with key constraints between UNC79-UNC80 and NALCN DI-DII and DII-DIII linkers informing a model of channelosome gating.

citation: Structure of the human sodium leak channel NALCN (PMID: 32698188)
summary: Cryo-EM structure of NALCN in complex with FAM155A shows that FAM155A forms an extracellular dome shielding the ion-selectivity filter from neurotoxin attack, and the channel has a tightly closed pore gate with occluded lateral fenestrations. Unusual voltage-sensor domains with asymmetric linkages to the pore suggest mechanisms for activity modulation. The majority of missense patient mutations causing gain-of-function phenotypes cluster around the S6 gate and distinctive π-bulges.

This demonstrates a role for NALCN in regulating the amount of REM sleep in vivo.

citation: The NALCN channel regulates metastasis and nonmalignant cell dissemination (PMID: 36175792)
sample_size: 10022 human cancers analyzed; multiple mouse models
summary: Deletion of Nalcn from gastric, intestinal, or pancreatic adenocarcinoma mouse models did not alter tumor incidence but markedly increased circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and metastases. Strikingly, deletion of Nalcn from non-tumor-bearing mice caused shedding of normal epithelial cells into the blood at levels equivalent to tumor-bearing animals, with these cells forming normal structures in distant organs, demonstrating NALCN regulates cell shedding from solid tissues independent of cancer.

citation: The NALCN Channel Regulator UNC-80 Functions in a Subset of Interneurons To Regulate Caenorhabditis elegans Reversal Behavior (PMID: 31690562)

Neuron-specific rescue and knockdown experiments demonstrated that command interneurons AVA and AVE and guidepost neuron AVG are sufficient for unc-80 regulation of reversal behavior, providing the first identification of key neurons in which the NALCN channelosome functions.

citation: Progesterone and estrogen regulate NALCN expression in human myometrial smooth muscle cells (PMID: 31935111)

Progesterone response elements (PREs), but not estrogen response elements, in the NALCN promoter contributed to this regulation as shown by luciferase assays, and E2/P4 correspondingly inhibited/enhanced an NALCN-dependent leak current in MSMCs.

citation: NALCN-mediated sodium influx confers metastatic prostate cancer cell invasiveness (PMID: 37278161)
summary: NALCN is overexpressed in metastatic prostate cancer cells and acts as a major initiator of Ca2+ oscillations required for invadopodia formation. NALCN-mediated Na+ influx maintains intracellular Ca2+ oscillations via plasmalemmal and mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchangers, SERCA, and store-operated channels, promoting Src kinase activity, actin remodeling, and secretion of proteolytic enzymes, thereby increasing invasive potential and metastatic lesions in vivo.

citation: The NALCN ion channel is a new actor in pancreatic β-cell physiology (PMID: 21099296)
summary: NALCN is expressed in rodent islets of Langerhans and the mouse MIN6 pancreatic β-cell line, where it mediates a cation current triggered by acetylcholine activation of M3 muscarinic receptors. The activation mechanism is independent of G protein action but dependent on a Src family kinase (SFK) pathway, and involves co-inclusion of M3 muscarinic receptors and NALCN in the same complex, revealing a novel role for NALCN in pancreatic β-cell excitability.

citation: NALCN expression is down-regulated and associated with immune infiltration in gastric cancer (PMID: 40013144)
summary: NALCN expression was significantly downregulated in gastric cancer (GC) tumor tissues and plasma compared to adjacent non-tumor tissues and healthy controls. NALCN knockdown in AGS and GES-1 GC cell lines markedly enhanced cell proliferation, colony formation, and migration while reducing apoptosis. TCGA analysis showed NALCN expression positively correlated with infiltration of B cells and CD8+ T cells and negatively with Th17 and Th2 cells; co-culture experiments showed NALCN knockdown in GC cells inhibited T cell proliferation.

citation: circADAMTS6 via stabilizing CAMK2A is involved in smoking-induced emphysema through driving M2 macrophage polarization (PMID: 38936066)
summary: In macrophages, circADAMTS6 stabilizes CAMK2A mRNA by forming a circADAMTS6/IGF2BP2/CAMK2A RNA-protein ternary complex, leading to CREB activation and M2 macrophage polarization. Downregulation of circADAMTS6 in mouse lung macrophages reversed M2 polarization and protected against cigarette smoke-induced emphysema, identifying CAMK2A as a key mediator in this non-neuronal inflammatory pathway.

citation: CaMK2A/CREB pathway activation is associated with enhanced mitophagy and neuronal apoptosis in diabetic retinopathy (PMID: 40216954)
summary: In a streptozotocin-induced diabetic retinopathy mouse model and high-glucose-treated retinal ganglion cells, CaMK2A/CREB pathway activation was associated with enhanced mitophagy and neuronal apoptosis. CaMK2A knockdown attenuated high-glucose-induced mitophagy, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while CREB activation exacerbated these effects, identifying CaMK2A as an upstream driver of mitophagy in this context.

citation: MicroRNA-3200-3p targeting CAMK2A modulates the proliferation and metastasis of glioma in vitro (PMID: 35287547)
summary: miR-3200-3p is downregulated in human glioma cells and directly targets CAMK2A; overexpression of CAMK2A reversed the anti-cancer effects of miR-3200-3p on glioma cell proliferation and metastasis. The mechanism involves CAMK2A regulation of the Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK pathway, implicating CAMK2A as a pro-tumorigenic factor in glioma.

citation: NF2 can mediate the expression of CAMK2A in a tissue specific manner (PMID: 39738767)
summary: Using KEGG analysis and CRISPR/Cas9 technology, NF2 was found to positively correlate with CAMK2A expression specifically in meningiomas and normal nervous system tissues, but not in non-nervous system tumors or tissues. This tissue-specific regulatory relationship suggests CAMK2A-related pathways mediate NF2's nervous system specificity and that targeting CAMK2A may be a therapeutic strategy for NF2-associated meningiomas.

citation: Lipophilic compounds restore function to neurodevelopmental-associated KCNQ3 mutations (PMID: 39300259)
summary: Using voltage clamp fluorometry, molecular dynamic simulations, and electrophysiology, two distinct loss- and gain-of-function mechanisms were identified for NDD-associated KCNQ3 variants: one affecting S4 voltage-sensor movement and another affecting S4-to-pore coupling. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) were shown to primarily target the voltage-sensing domain in its activated conformation, and two PUFA compounds yielded partial and complete functional restoration in R227Q- and R236C-containing KCNQ3 channels, respectively.

citation: Electrophysiological Abnormalities and Pharmacological Corrections of Pathogenic Missense Variants in KCNQ3 (PMID: 40095209)
summary: A library of 24 missense KCNQ3 mutations was introduced into three channel backgrounds (KCNQ3, KCNQ3-A315T, and KCNQ3-KCNQ2 tandem) and analyzed by patch-clamp recording. Loss-of-function mutations concentrated in the pore-forming domain were associated with self-limited familial neonatal epilepsy, while gain-of-function mutations (leftward V1/2 shifts) were associated with neurodevelopmental disorders; the KCNQ opener Pynegabine reversed LOF mutations and the KCNQ inhibitor Amitriptyline reversed GOF mutations including the novel G553R variant.

citation: KCNQ2/3 Gain-of-Function Variants and Cell Excitability: Differential Effects in CA1 versus L2/3 Pyramidal Neurons (PMID: 37607817)

These cell-type-specific effects reveal that KCNQ3 gain-of-function impacts neuronal excitability in a brain-region- and cell-type-dependent manner.

In four children with gain-of-function KCNQ3 variants (p.Arg227Gln, p.Arg230Cys), off-label donepezil treatment for 12 months produced clinically significant improvement in autism symptoms in two patients.

citation: Increased KCNQ3 expression in papillary thyroid cancer promotes proliferation and migration (PMID: 41250218)
summary: KCNQ3 was found to be aberrantly overexpressed in papillary thyroid cancer and mechanistically interacts with GAREM1, GRB2, and SOS1 (identified by co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry), activating the RAS/RAF/MAPK signaling cascade to promote tumor cell proliferation and migration. ChIP-qPCR revealed that estradiol (E2) enhances KCNQ3 transcription via estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) binding to the KCNQ3 promoter, and the KCNQ channel inhibitor XE991 inhibited PTC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and in vivo.

citation: DNA methylation and expression of KCNQ3 in bipolar disorder (PMID: 25041603)
sample_size: BPD cases and matched controls from McLean Hospital + Stanley Medical Research Institute cohort
summary: In postmortem prefrontal cortex from bipolar disorder patients, KCNQ3 mRNA expression was significantly lower compared to matched controls, and DNA methylation at CpGs within KCNQ3 exon 11 was significantly reduced in BPD, correlating with KCNQ3 mRNA levels. Replication in the Stanley Medical Research Institute cohort confirmed lower KCNQ3 exon 11 methylation after correcting for mood stabilizer status, suggesting epigenetic dysregulation of KCNQ3 in BPD pathogenesis.

citation: Molecular and circuit determinants in the globus pallidus mediating control of cocaine-induced behavioral plasticity (PMID: 39153478)
summary: In the globus pallidus externus (GPe), expression of KCNQ3 and KCNQ5 voltage-gated potassium channels was downregulated following cocaine exposure in parvalbumin-positive (GPePV) neurons, contributing to elevated GPePV cell excitability. Acute activation of KCNQ3/KCNQ5-containing channels with carnosic acid reduced GPePV excitability and impaired cocaine reward, sensitization, and volitional cocaine intake in mice.

citation: Transcriptional control of KCNQ channel genes and the regulation of neuronal excitability (PMID: 20926649)
summary: The transcription factor Sp1 activates KCNQ3 expression, while the transcriptional repressor REST represses KCNQ3 expression, establishing two key regulatory mechanisms controlling KCNQ3 mRNA levels. Transcriptional regulation of KCNQ3 was mirrored by correlated changes in M-current density and excitability in native sensory neurons, implicating these pathways in seizure activity and pain.

citation: SMAD4 and KCNQ3 alterations are associated with lymph node metastases in oesophageal adenocarcinoma (PMID: 37648039)
summary: Transcriptomic analysis of oesophageal adenocarcinoma identified KCNQ3 as associated with lymph node metastasis, with KCNQ3 uniquely linked to changes in planar cell polarity associated with non-canonical Wnt signaling (distinct from SMAD4's association with canonical Wnt). Overexpression of KCNQ3 in cell line and xenograft systems reduced wound closure and the number of metastases observed, suggesting a functional role in suppressing metastatic behavior.

citation: KCNQ2 and KCNQ5 form heteromeric channels independent of KCNQ3 (PMID: 35320039)
summary: Using split-intein protein trans-splicing to form KCNQ2/5 tandems and mass spectrometry of native brain channels, KCNQ2 was shown to associate with KCNQ5 in the brain even in the absence of KCNQ3, demonstrating that KCNQ channel composition is more diverse than the previously assumed KCNQ2/3 or KCNQ3/5 heteromers. Functional heterologous expression data were also consistent with the formation of KCNQ2/3/5 heteromers, necessitating re-examination of genotype/phenotype relationships for KCNQ3-containing channels.

citation: Auto-fatty acylation of transcription factor RFX3 regulates ciliogenesis. (PMID: 30127002)
summary: RFX3 undergoes enzyme-independent auto-S-fatty acylation at a conserved cysteine in its dimerization domain, preferring 18-carbon stearic and oleic acids. A fatty acylation-deficient RFX3 mutant shows decreased homodimerization, fails to promote ciliary gene expression and ciliogenesis, and impairs Hedgehog signaling. This links fatty acid metabolism and protein lipidation to RFX3-mediated regulation of ciliogenesis.

citation: Multi-omic analysis of the ciliogenic transcription factor RFX3 reveals a role in promoting activity-dependent responses via enhancing CREB binding in human neurons. (PMID: 40060598)
summary: Using human iPSC-derived neurons and forebrain organoids, biallelic loss of RFX3 disrupted ciliary gene expression and delayed neuronal differentiation, while monoallelic loss disrupted synaptic target gene expression and diminished activity-dependent gene expression. RFX3 binding sites co-localized with CREB binding sites near activity-dependent genes, and RFX3 deficiency led to decreased CREB binding and impaired induction of CREB targets upon neuronal depolarization. This reveals a novel role for RFX3 in shaping neuronal synaptic development and plasticity relevant to ASD.

citation: RFX3 is essential for the generation of functional human pancreatic islets from stem cells. (PMID: 40263183)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of RFX3 in human iPSCs differentiated into pancreatic islet organoids reduced hormone-secreting islet cells, impaired beta cell function and insulin secretion, increased apoptosis, and elevated enterochromaffin cell markers. RFX3 overexpression rescued dysregulated gene expression in RFX3 KO cells at pancreatic progenitor and endocrine progenitor stages. These findings establish RFX3 as essential for human islet cell differentiation and suppression of enterochromaffin cell specification.

citation: The transcription factor Rfx3 regulates beta-cell differentiation, function, and glucokinase expression. (PMID: 20413507)
summary: In Rfx3-deficient mice, reduced insulin-positive beta-cells resulted from accumulation of incompletely differentiated beta-cell precursors with reduced insulin, Glut-2, and glucokinase (Gck) expression, leading to glucose intolerance in adults. ChIP and bandshift experiments showed Rfx3 binds the Pal-1 and Pal-2 regulatory sequences in the neuroendocrine promoter of the glucokinase gene in Min6 cells and human islets. RNAi-mediated knockdown of Rfx3 in Min6 beta-cells also attenuated Glut-2 and glucokinase expression and impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

citation: The transcription factor RFX3 directs nodal cilium development and left-right asymmetry specification. (PMID: 15121860)
summary: Rfx3-knockout mice exhibit frequent left-right asymmetry defects, situs inversus, and high embryonic lethality due to stunted nodal monocilia. RFX3 is expressed in ciliated cells of the embryonic node and regulates expression of D2lic, the mouse orthologue of a C. elegans intraflagellar transport gene. This establishes RFX3 as essential for nodal monocilia differentiation and left-right body axis determination in mammals.

citation: RFX3 governs growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia in mouse and controls the expression of genes involved in human ciliopathies. (PMID: 19671664)
summary: Using primary multiciliated cells from mouse brain, Rfx3-deficient cells showed impaired growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia. RFX3 was required for optimal FOXJ1 expression and directly bound promoters of axonemal dynein genes involved in ciliary motility. This demonstrates RFX3 regulates both ciliary assembly and motility genes associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia in humans.

citation: RFX3 modulation of FOXJ1 regulation of cilia genes in the human airway epithelium. (PMID: 23822649)
summary: In primary human airway basal cells, transfection of RFX3 alone did not induce cilia-related gene expression, but the combination of FOXJ1 and RFX3 enhanced ciliated gene promoter activity and mRNA expression beyond FOXJ1 alone. Co-immunoprecipitation studies demonstrated a physical interaction between FOXJ1 and RFX3 proteins. RFX3 thus acts as a transcriptional co-activator to FOXJ1 during ciliated cell differentiation of airway basal/progenitor cells.

citation: Disruption of RFX family transcription factors causes autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, intellectual disability, and dysregulated behavior. (PMID: 33658631)
summary: RFX3 (along with RFX4 and RFX7) is strongly expressed in developing and adult human brain. X-box binding motifs and RFX ChIP-seq peaks are enriched in cis-regulatory regions of known ASD risk genes. A cohort of 38 individuals with de novo variants in RFX3, RFX4, and RFX7 share neurobehavioral features including ASD, intellectual disability, and/or ADHD, establishing RFX3 as a critical transcriptional regulator of neurobiological pathways associated with neurodevelopmental disease.

citation: Histone H2B monoubiquitination regulates heart development via epigenetic control of cilia motility. (PMID: 31235600)
summary: ChIP-seq of mouse ciliated and non-ciliated tissues showed tissue-specific H2B monoubiquitination (H2Bub1) marks significantly enriched at the Rfx3 locus. Rnf20 knockdown in Xenopus reduced rfx3 mRNA levels and caused abnormal heart looping and defective left-right asymmetry, which was rescued by exogenous rfx3. This places RFX3 downstream of the RNF20/H2Bub1 chromatin remodeling pathway as a key mediator of cilia-dependent cardiac situs determination.

citation: Downregulation of microRNA-342-3p Eases Insulin Resistance and Liver Gluconeogenesis via Regulating Rfx3 in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus. (PMID: 35997120)
summary: In a streptozocin-induced GDM mouse model, miR-342-3p was upregulated and Rfx3 was downregulated in placenta and pancreatic tissues; dual luciferase assays confirmed miR-342-3p directly targets the Rfx3 3'-UTR. Knockdown of miR-342-3p decreased blood glucose, reduced apoptosis, and alleviated insulin resistance and liver gluconeogenesis, effects that were reversed by Rfx3 silencing. This identifies a miR-342-3p/Rfx3 regulatory axis relevant to gestational diabetes pathophysiology.

summary: GABRA1 (the α1 subunit of GABAA receptor) is expressed in dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV) neurons and mediates the effect of puerarin on intestinal fat absorption. citation: An airway-to-brain sensory pathway mediates influenza-induced sickness (PMID: 36890237)
summary: GABRA1 is expressed in a specific subpopulation of glossopharyngeal sensory neurons (petrosal GABRA1 neurons) that detect PGE2 and mediate influenza-induced sickness behavior in mice. Ablation of petrosal GABRA1 neurons or targeted knockout of the PGE2 receptor EP3 in these neurons eliminated influenza-induced decreases in food intake, water intake, and mobility. These neurons project to mucosal regions of the nasopharynx and display specific axonal targeting in the brainstem.

citation: Understanding paralogous epilepsy-associated GABA(A) receptor variants (PMID: 39642202)

citation: Synaptic clustering differences due to different GABRB3 mutations cause variable epilepsy syndromes (PMID: 31435640)

citation: Gain-of-function GABRB3 variants identified in vigabatrin-hypersensitive epileptic encephalopathies (PMID: 33585817)

citation: A Novel De Novo Gain-of-Function CACNA1D Variant in Neurodevelopmental Disease With Congenital Tremor, Seizures, and Hypotonia (PMID: 39246741)
summary: Patch-clamp electrophysiology of the p.(G1169D) CACNA1D variant in tsA201 cells revealed pronounced activity-enhancing gating changes, including shifts of channel activation and inactivation to more hyperpolarized potentials, as well as impaired channel inactivation and deactivation. This gain-of-function variant was identified de novo in two children with neurodevelopmental disease of variable severity. The variant retained sensitivity to the Ca2+ channel blocker isradipine in vitro, though no beneficial clinical effects were observed.

citation: CACNA1D-Related Channelopathies: From Hypertension to Autism (PMID: 36592224)
summary: CACNA1D encodes the pore-forming α1 subunit of Cav1.3 L-type voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; loss of function causes deafness and bradycardia, while de novo gain-of-function missense variants cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome including autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, primary aldosteronism, and hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. In vitro electrophysiological studies of multiple de novo variants revealed activity-enhancing gating changes consistent with enhanced Ca2+ influx as the disease mechanism. Dihydropyridine L-type Ca2+ channel blockers have been explored as potential therapeutic options.

citation: CACNA1D overexpression and voltage-gated calcium channels in prostate cancer during androgen deprivation (PMID: 36949059)
summary: CACNA1D and CaV1.3 protein are overexpressed in prostate tumours; in androgen-sensitive LNCaP cells, androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) or enzalutamide treatment increased CACNA1D expression and enabled depolarization/Bay K 8644-evoked nifedipine-sensitive Ca2+ transients and detectable CaV1.3 currents. CACNA1D knockdown reduced the subpopulation of treated LNCaP cells with CaV1.3 activity. These findings suggest that physiological and genomic CACNA1D/CaV1.3 mechanisms become active during hormone therapy in prostate cancer.

citation: Nutrient-sensitizing drug repurposing screen identifies lomerizine as a mitochondrial metabolism inhibitor of chronic myeloid leukemia (PMID: 38865484)
summary: Transcriptome analysis revealed increased expression of voltage-gated CACNA1D in CML leukemic stem cells (CD34+CD38-) compared with normal counterparts, correlating with increased ER mass and elevated ER and mitochondrial Ca2+ content. CACNA1D knockdown in CML cells led to ER and mitochondrial Ca2+ depletion, inhibited mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase activity, and sensitized CML LSCs to imatinib treatment. These findings implicate CACNA1D-mediated Ca2+ influx in supporting mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in CML stem cells.

citation: Dominant role of CACNA1D exon mutations for blood pressure regulation (PMID: 35142739)
summary: CRISPR-Cas9-engineered Sprague-Dawley rats carrying the CACNA1D p.D307G mutation showed elevated systolic blood pressure, increased circulating ET-1, and vascular/cardiac/renal remodeling over 32 weeks. Increased Cav1.3 protein expression and calcineurin phosphatase activity were observed in VSMCs, and ET-1 expression was elevated in aortic endothelial cells from mutant rats. Double heterozygosity (p.D307G/p.R1516Q or p.D307G/p.V936I) further accelerated SBP rise, and isradipine or BQ-123 reduced BP in double-mutant rats.

citation: CaBP1 and 2 enable sustained CaV1.3 calcium currents and synaptic transmission in inner hair cells (PMID: 39718549)
summary: In Cabp1/2 double-knockout mice, CaV1.3 (encoded by CACNA1D) showed strongly enhanced inactivation, slowed recovery from inactivation, and impaired sustained exocytosis at inner hair cell ribbon synapses. Spontaneous and sound-evoked responses of spiral ganglion neurons were strikingly reduced, demonstrating that CaBP1 and CaBP2 cooperatively suppress voltage- and calcium-dependent inactivation of IHC CaV1.3 channels to support fast, temporally precise sound encoding. Transgenic expression of CaBP2 substantially rescued IHC synaptic function and hearing sensitivity.

citation: Genetic causes of primary aldosteronism (PMID: 31695023)
summary: Somatic driver mutations in CACNA1D (encoding the α1 subunit of L-type voltage-gated calcium channel CaV1.3) are found in a substantial portion of aldosterone-producing adenomas, implicating intracellular calcium signaling as a key pathway in aldosterone overproduction. Rare germline variants of CACNA1D have also been reported in familial hyperaldosteronism. These mutations lead to altered ion transport, cell membrane depolarization, activation of voltage-gated calcium channels, and increased aldosterone synthase transcription.

citation: ASHG 2017 - African ancestry genome- and transcriptome-wide association study of blood pressure detects nine novel loci in a large cohort from the Million Veteran Program

This finding identifies CACNA1D as a novel locus for diastolic blood pressure in African Americans. Transcriptome-wide association analysis suggested that reduced expression of nearby TMEM110 in nucleus accumbens-basal ganglia may be the relevant functional signal for the SBP association in that region.

citation: ASHG 2015 - Epigenomic profiling of prostate cancer identifies differentially methylated genes in TMPRSS2:ERG fusion positive versus negative tumors

citation: ASHG 2014 - Exome analyses reveal new autism genes in synaptic, transcriptional, and chromatin networks

The study implicated synaptic development as a major theme in ASD risk, with CACNA1D as a key voltage-gated ion channel component.

citation: Comprehensive EHMT1 variants analysis broadens genotype-phenotype associations and molecular mechanisms in Kleefstra syndrome (PMID: 39013458)
summary: EHMT1 encodes euchromatic histone methyltransferase-1, a pivotal epigenetic machinery component. Disruption of the ankyrin repeat domain 'reader' function produces a Kleefstra syndrome-specific DNA methylation signature and milder phenotype, while disruption of only the SET domain 'writer' methyltransferase activity does not produce the DNAm signature or typical phenotype. N-terminal truncating variants result in a mild phenotype without the DNAm signature, revealing distinct genotype-phenotype associations tied to specific protein domains.

citation: An epigenetic barrier sets the timing of human neuronal maturation (PMID: 38297124)
summary: Transient inhibition of EHMT1 (along with EZH2/EHMT2 or DOT1L) at the progenitor stage in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cortical neurons enables precocious neuronal maturation, demonstrating that EHMT1 is part of an epigenetic barrier in progenitor cells that holds transcriptional maturation programmes in a poised state. Loss of function of EHMT1 in cortical neurons allows newly born neurons to rapidly acquire mature properties upon differentiation. This identifies EHMT1 as a cell-intrinsic regulator of the prolonged timeline of human cortical neuron maturation.

citation: Two conserved epigenetic regulators prevent healthy ageing (PMID: 32103178)
summary: Genome-wide RNAi screening in C. elegans identified SET-6, the ortholog of EHMT1, as a neuronal H3K9 methyltransferase that accelerates behavioral deterioration in aging worms by reducing mitochondrial function and repressing nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins. This mechanism was conserved in cultured mouse neurons and human cells. Human EHMT1 expression in the frontal cortex increases with age and correlates positively with Alzheimer's disease progression.

citation: EHMT1 and EHMT2 inhibition induces fetal hemoglobin expression (PMID: 26320100)
summary: Pharmacological inhibition of EHMT1/2 with UNC0638 and shRNA-mediated knockdown of EHMT1 or EHMT2 in primary human adult erythroid cells significantly increased γ-globin expression, HbF synthesis, and the percentage of HbF-expressing cells. ChIP-seq revealed genome-wide depletion of the repressive H3K9me2 mark and a concomitant increase in activating H3K9Ac, especially pronounced at the γ-globin gene region. These findings establish EHMT1 and EHMT2 as epigenetic repressors of γ-globin and potential therapeutic targets for sickle cell disease.

citation: Distinct functions of EHMT1 and EHMT2 in cancer chemotherapy and immunotherapy (PMID: 37873068)
summary: EHMT1-mediated methylation of the non-histone substrate LIG1 (DNA ligase 1) is responsible for effects on DNA replication fork progression and sensitivity to alkylating chemotherapy, while EHMT2 activity regulates STING expression via CpG demethylation at the STING1 promoter. EHMT1/2 inhibition causes ATM-mediated replication fork slowdown, accumulation of single-stranded gaps, and cytosolic DNA emergence. These results highlight distinct, non-redundant functions of the two paralogs in DNA replication and immune signaling.

citation: The Histone Methyltransferases EHMT1 and EHMT2 Repress the Expression of Genes Related to Excitability and Cell Death in Oligodendrocyte Progenitors (PMID: 40134232)
summary: The repressive H3K9me2 histone mark deposited by EHMT1 and EHMT2 increases in proliferating oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in mice following optogenetic stimulation of neuronal activity. Genetic deletion of Ehmt1 and Ehmt2 in OPCs leads to higher levels of cholinergic muscarinic receptors, fewer oligodendrocyte lineage cells, and lower myelin basic protein levels. EHMT1/2 are thus required to repress genes regulating cell death and electrical properties in proliferating OPCs.

citation: EHMT1 mediates cellular motility in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma by activating SOX8 expression (PMID: 40467997)
summary: EHMT1 depletion in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (ERMS) cells reduced migration and invasion in vitro and metastasis in vivo in a mouse xenograft model. Mechanistically, EHMT1 upregulates the transcription factor SOX8 by regulating BRD4 expression and increasing BRD4 occupancy at the SOX8 promoter, which in turn activates integrin gene expression. This identifies a novel EHMT1-BRD4-SOX8 axis mediating metastasis in ERMS.

citation: BRD4 acts as a transcriptional repressor of RhoB to inhibit terminal erythropoiesis (PMID: 40598222)
summary: ChIP-qPCR and co-immunoprecipitation studies revealed that BRD4 acts as a transcriptional repressor by physically interacting with the histone methyltransferases EHMT1 and EHMT2 at the RhoB locus in erythroblasts. This non-classical BRD4 function, dependent on its interaction with EHMT1/2, represses RhoB expression and disrupts actin reorganization to inhibit terminal erythropoiesis. The study identifies EHMT1/2 as co-repressors in a BRD4-containing complex regulating erythroid maturation.

citation: Cell consequences of loss of function of the epigenetic factor EHMT1 (PMID: 37257768)
summary: EHMT1 depletion in RPE1 cells caused alterations in morphology and distribution of the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and cell adhesion components, and increased centriolar satellite detection suggesting a role in centrosome functioning. EHMT1-depleted cells also showed reduced migration capacity. These cellular phenotypes provide mechanistic insights into how EHMT1 haploinsufficiency may contribute to the neurodevelopmental features of Kleefstra syndrome.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Identification of three novel genes for Kleefstra syndrome associated phenotypes establishes a chromatin modification module of the EHMT1 gene network (T. Kleefstra et al.)
summary: Disruption of EHMT1 in Drosophila melanogaster resulted in a developmental phenotype including impaired neurodevelopment and defects in learning and memory. Genetic interaction studies between EHMT1 and novel Kleefstra syndrome-associated chromatin modifier genes revealed reciprocal modulation of mutant phenotypes, providing evidence for functional interaction within an EHMT1 chromatin modification module. EHMT1 protein functions through mono- and dimethylation of H3K9 in euchromatic regions to modulate gene expression during neuronal development.

summary: Ten individuals with intellectual disability, speech delay, ataxia, and facial dysmorphism carried de novo or mosaic EBF3 variants; mutant EBF3 proteins showed cytoplasmic mislocalization, reduced chromatin association, and significantly reduced or absent transcriptional activation of CDKN1A. RNA-seq and ChIP-seq demonstrated that EBF3 acts as a transcriptional regulator with reduced genome-wide DNA binding and gene-regulatory activity in mutants. EBF3 variants are estimated to be present in ~0.1% of individuals with unexplained neurodevelopmental disorders.

citation: Stem cell niche-specific Ebf3 maintains the bone marrow cavity (PMID: 29563184)
summary: Ebf3 is preferentially expressed in CAR/LepR+ mesenchymal stem cells within bone marrow, and lineage tracing showed Ebf3-expressing cells are self-renewing mesenchymal stem cells. Deletion of Ebf3 in CAR/LepR+ cells severely impaired HSC niche function and caused osteosclerosis with increased bone in aged mice. Combined loss of Ebf1 and Ebf3 led to depletion of HSCs and progressive occlusion of marrow cavities, demonstrating Ebf3 is required to inhibit osteoblast differentiation and maintain HSC niches.

citation: Prdm13 is required for Ebf3+ amacrine cell formation in the retina (PMID: 29258872)
summary: Ebf3 is expressed in a subset of amacrine interneurons in the adult mouse retina, co-expressed with calretinin in most Prdm13+ amacrine cells. Loss of Prdm13 resulted in a 25% reduction in amacrine cells and complete absence of Ebf3+ amacrine cell subtypes in adult mice. These findings establish Ebf3 as a marker of a specific amacrine cell subtype whose formation depends on Prdm13.

citation: Transient and lineage-restricted requirement of Ebf3 for sternum ossification (PMID: 32398354)
summary: Ebf3 marks tenocytes and connective tissue cells in zebrafish embryos, and knockout of Ebf3 in mice causes sternum ossification defects due to defective generation of Runx2+ pre-osteoblasts without affecting chondrogenesis. Conditional knockout revealed Ebf3 is required in lateral plate mesenchyme cells, particularly tendon/muscle connective tissue cells, at embryonic day 9.5–10.5. Ebf3 deletion led to upregulation of connective tissue markers (Egr1/2, Osr1), increased Islet1+ mesenchyme cells, and downregulation of the Runx2 regulator Shox2.

citation: An Integrated Phenotypic and Genotypic Approach Reveals a High-Risk Subtype Association for EBF3 Missense Variants Affecting the Zinc Finger Domain (PMID: 35340043)
summary: In vivo Drosophila UAS-GAL4 expression assays showed that EBF3 missense variants disrupting the zinc finger domain (ZNF) failed to restore viability, while the recurrent DBD variant p.Arg209Trp partially rescued viability. In vitro luciferase assays confirmed that ZNF-associated variants impaired transcriptional activation, whereas p.Arg209Trp preserved partial transcriptional activity. Phenotypic assessment of 83 EBF3-NDD individuals demonstrated that ZNF variants correlate with greater symptom severity.

citation: Coding and noncoding variants in EBF3 are involved in HADDS and simplex autism (PMID: 34256850)
significance: missense p=8.12×10⁻³⁵; LoF p=2.26×10⁻¹³; enhancer combined p=1.1×10⁻⁴
summary: De novo variants in the brain-specific enhancer hs737, which targets EBF3 in human fetal brain, were identified in autism families; in vitro assays in a neuronal cell line showed all tested DNVs reduced enhancer activity. EBF3 is genome-wide significant for coding de novo variants in NDDs (missense p=8.12×10⁻³⁵, LoF p=2.26×10⁻¹³), and ChIP-seq in neuronal cells showed EBF3 promoter binding is enriched for NDD genes (p=7.43×10⁻⁶, OR=1.87). Individuals with coding DNVs had greater phenotypic severity (HADDS) compared to those with noncoding enhancer DNVs who presented with autism and hypotonia.

citation: Early B Cell Factor 3 (EBF3) attenuates Parkinson's disease through directly regulating contactin-associated protein-like 4 (CNTNAP4) transcription: An experimental study (PMID: 38479556)
summary: EBF3 expression is downregulated in the substantia nigra of MPTP-induced PD mice and MPP+-treated SH-SY5Y cells, associated with reduced m6A methylation. EBF3 overexpression ameliorated behavioral deficits in PD mice, suppressed neuronal apoptosis in vivo, and protected SH-SY5Y cells from MPP+-induced apoptosis by restoring mitochondrial function. Luciferase reporter, ChIP, and DNA pull-down assays confirmed EBF3 directly binds the CNTNAP4 promoter to activate its transcription, and CNTNAP4 knockdown abolished EBF3's neuroprotective effects.

citation: Loss of Notch signaling in skeletal stem cells enhances bone formation with aging (PMID: 37752132)
summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified Ebf3 as a downstream mediator of Notch signaling in skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) that is dysregulated with aging. Deletion of Nicastrin (an essential Notch pathway component) in SSPCs led to elevated osteo-lineage gene expression and increased bone mass, with Ebf3 identified as a key transcriptional target in this pathway. Ebf3 is highlighted as a promising therapeutic target to rejuvenate the aged skeleton by modulating SSPC cell fate decisions.

citation: Aberrant DNA methylation and tumor suppressive activity of the EBF3 gene in gastric carcinoma (PMID: 21387304)
summary: EBF3 promoter hypermethylation was detected in 40.4% (42/104) of gastric cancer tissues but not in normal gastric tissues, and EBF3 was reactivated by 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine and/or trichostatin A in all ten gastric cancer cell lines tested. siRNA knockdown and cDNA transfection experiments demonstrated that EBF3 represses gastric cancer cell growth and migration while activating cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. EBF3 promoter methylation correlated significantly with lymphatic invasion (p=0.013) and poor survival (p=0.038), supporting its role as an independent prognostic marker.
