summary: In wild-type larval zebrafish, kcnb1 was expressed in various regions of the central nervous system including neurons, oligodendrocytes, and microglial cells. Both kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/- zebrafish displayed impaired swimming behavior and epilepsy-like features restored by human Kv2.1 WT DNA. The kcnb1-/- model showed spontaneous and provoked epileptiform-like electrographic activity associated with GABA dysregulation, with increased bdnf mRNA and c-Fos fluorescence in the telencephalon upon PTZ exposure.

citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
summary: The KCNB1-p.G379R variant was shown to have a dominant-negative effect on KV2.1 clustering at endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions in HEK293T cells. Kcnb1G379R knock-in mice exhibited spontaneous seizures, hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, impulsivity, reduced anxiety, and abnormal interictal EEG activity. Immunohistochemistry revealed genotype-dependent reductions in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression, confirming both conducting and non-conducting (structural) roles of KCNB1.

citation: Integrin-KCNB1 potassium channel complexes regulate neocortical neuronal development and are implicated in epilepsy (PMID: 36207442)
summary: KCNB1 forms complexes with integrins α5β5 (Integrin-K+ channel Complexes, IKCs) in neocortical neurons, and biochemical signaling of these complexes was impaired in Kcnb1-R312H knock-in mice. KCNB1 null mice showed impaired neuronal migration of glutamatergic neurons, disrupted morphology, synaptic connectivity defects, seizures, anxiety, and compulsive behavior. Treatment with Angiotensin II (a Focal Adhesion kinase agonist) in vitro corrected the neuronal abnormalities, demonstrating a non-conducting developmental role for KCNB1 via IKC signaling.

citation: KCNB1-Leptin receptor complexes couple electric and endocrine function in the melanocortin neurons of the hypothalamus (PMID: 39436109)
summary: KCNB1 (Kv2.1) forms stable complexes with the leptin receptor (LepR) in hypothalamic neurons including POMC-expressing neurons of the Arcuate nucleus. Mice lacking functional KCNB1 channels had less adipose tissue, lower circulating leptin, insensitivity to leptin-induced anorexia, and aberrant POMC production. Canonical LepR-STAT3 signaling was impaired while non-canonical PI3K/Akt/FOXO1 and ERK signaling were constitutively upregulated, establishing KCNB1 as a molecular link between neuronal excitability and endocrine function.

citation: Functions and clinical significance of KCNB1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 39893596)
summary: siRNA knockdown of KCNB1 in human ESCC cell lines (KYSE70 and TE5) inhibited cell proliferation, G2-M phase progression, migration, and invasion, and induced apoptosis. Microarray analysis showed KCNB1 regulates Ephrin receptor signaling by suppressing EPHB1, EPHB2, and ERK1/2 gene expression. Immunohistochemical analysis of 129 primary ESCC tumor samples identified high KCNB1 expression as an independent prognostic factor for poor 5-year relapse-free survival.

citation: Antagonistic roles of Ras-MAPK and Akt signaling in integrin-K(+) channel complex-mediated cellular apoptosis (PMID: 35357039)
summary: In response to oxidative stress, IKCs (complexes of α5-integrins and KCNB1/Kv2.1) activate an apoptotic Ras-MAPK/ERK signaling pathway. Simultaneously, wild-type KCNB1 channels sequester Akt, causing dephosphorylation of BAD and promoting apoptosis, whereas the C73A KCNB1 variant that does not induce apoptosis does not sequester Akt. These findings place KCNB1 at the intersection of pro-apoptotic Ras-MAPK and pro-survival Akt signaling pathways.

citation: Spectrum of K(V) 2.1 Dysfunction in KCNB1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorders (PMID: 31600826)
summary: High-throughput functional screening of 17 KCNB1 variants associated with DEE or other NDDs revealed diverse molecular defects including altered current density, shifts in voltage dependence of activation/inactivation, reduced total KV2.1 expression, and deficient cell-surface expression. Pathogenic variants exhibited these defects both as homotetramers and when co-expressed with wild-type KV2.1. This established a platform for rapid screening of KV2.1 functional defects and demonstrated that KCNB1 variants cause dysfunction through multiple distinct mechanisms.

citation: Gain-of-function enhancer variant near KCNB1 causes familial ST-depression syndrome (PMID: 40208226)
summary: A rare non-coding variant located 18 kb downstream of KCNB1 on chromosome 20 was identified in all affected individuals across 20 families with familial ST-depression syndrome (FSTD), with full penetrance and autosomal dominant inheritance. The variant creates a MEF2-binding site that enhances transcriptional activity, and 4C chromosome conformation capture confirmed direct interaction between this locus and the KCNB1 promoter in AC16 cardiomyocytes and human muscle tissue. dCas9-activator/repressor assays showed KCNB1 was the only gene consistently regulated by the locus, implicating KCNB1 for the first time in human cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.

citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation (PMID: 28144039)
summary: KCNB1 expression was associated with favorable overall survival and progression-free survival in glioma patients across three datasets (CGGA, GSE16011, REMBRANDT). In vitro studies showed KCNB1 induces autophagy accompanied by increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation and invasion of glioma cells via the ERK pathway, confirmed by inhibition with a selective ERK1/2 inhibitor (U0126) or siERK1/2. In vivo studies confirmed KCNB1-induced autophagy inhibited tumor growth and increased survival.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic variants in KCNB1 are modestly associated with type 2 diabetes in American Indians from the Gila River Indian Community
summary: An intronic 16 bp deletion in KCNB1 (MAF=0.02) was associated with protection from type 2 diabetes in 7,351 Pima Indians (OR=0.51, p=1.2×10⁻³). A common variant rs3827088 (MAF=0.31) was also nominally associated with T2D and replicated in an independent cohort of 3,004 American Indians (combined N=10,448, OR=1.18, p=2.5×10⁻⁴). Conditional analysis suggested the two variants have independent effects on T2D risk, consistent with KCNB1's known role in regulating insulin secretion.

citation: Ae4 (Slc4a9) is an electroneutral monovalent cation-dependent Cl-/HCO3- exchanger (PMID: 27114614)
summary: Native Ae4 activity in mouse salivary gland acinar cells and heterologous expression in CHO-K1 cells demonstrates that Ae4 is an electroneutral Cl-/nonselective cation-HCO3- exchanger, transporting Na+ in the same direction as HCO3- and opposite to Cl-. citation: The forkhead transcription factor Foxi1 directly activates the AE4 promoter (PMID: 16159312)
summary: The forkhead transcription factor Foxi1 directly activates the Slc4a9 (AE4) promoter approximately 100-fold in cell-based reporter gene assays, with a minimal 462 bp upstream fragment sufficient for activation. A single Foxi1 binding site within this region was identified by bandshift assays, and its mutation abolished both Foxi1 binding and transcriptional activation, establishing Slc4a9 as a direct Foxi1 target gene in type B intercalated cells.

citation: Insights into acidosis-induced regulation of SLC26A4 (pendrin) and SLC4A9 (AE4) transporters using three-dimensional morphometric analysis of β-intercalated cells (PMID: 24990900)
summary: AE4 (SLC4A9) is expressed as a barrel-like structure in the lateral membrane of β-intercalated cells in the rabbit cortical collecting duct, consistent with a role in basolateral Na+-HCO3- cotransport. Acidosis significantly reduced AE4 expression in β-intercalated cells, which was rapidly reversed during recovery from acidosis, indicating coordinate regulation with pendrin during acid-base disturbances.

citation: Disrupting Hypoxia-Induced Bicarbonate Transport Acidifies Tumor Cells and Suppresses Tumor Growth (PMID: 27197160)
summary: Hypoxia induced SLC4A9 expression in cancer cell lines in a HIF1α- and HIF2α-dependent manner. RNAi-mediated attenuation of SLC4A9 acidified intracellular pH, increased apoptosis in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer spheroids, and dramatically reduced growth of MDA-MB-231 breast tumors and U87 gliomas in murine xenografts.

citation: Integrated compensatory network is activated in the absence of NCC phosphorylation (PMID: 25893600)
summary: In SPAK kinase-deficient mice unable to activate the thiazide-sensitive NCC cotransporter, global transcriptional profiling revealed coordinate induction of Slc4a9 along with Slc26a4 and Slc4a8 in pendrin-positive intercalated cells as part of a compensatory salt reabsorption pathway. This multigene transport system, together with carbonic anhydrase isoforms and V-type H+-ATPase subunits, establishes adaptive NaCl reabsorption in the distal nephron.

citation: The transcription factor Foxi1 promotes expression of V-ATPase and Gpr116 in M-1 cells (PMID: 36603001)
summary: Overexpression of the transcription factor Foxi1 in M-1 murine cortical collecting duct cells induced expression of Slc4a9 along with other intercalated cell markers including Gpr116, Atp6v1b1, Atp6v1g3, Atp6v0d2, and Slc26a4. citation: Somatic SETBP1 mutations in myeloid neoplasms (PMID: 28447248)
summary: SETBP1 is a SET-binding protein that regulates self-renewal potential through HOXA-protein activation. Mutant SETBP1 attenuates RUNX1 and activates MYB, and mouse models confirmed biological significance of SETBP1 mutations in myeloid leukemogenesis, particularly in cooperation with ASXL1 mutations. Somatic hotspot mutations prevent proteasomal degradation, leading to SETBP1 protein accumulation and downstream oncogenic signaling.

citation: The m(6)A methyltransferase METTL14 promotes cell proliferation via SETBP1-mediated activation of PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in myelodysplastic neoplasms (PMID: 39054337)

Knockdown of METTL14 inhibited cell proliferation and colony formation, and in vivo experiments showed reduced tumor burden and prolonged survival. This identifies a METTL14/m6A/SETBP1/PI3K-AKT signaling axis in MDS pathogenesis.

citation: The landscape of SETBP1 gene expression and transcription factor activity across human tissues (PMID: 37873221)
summary: SETBP1 and its known target genes are widely expressed across 31 adult human tissues based on GTEx RNA-seq data. K-means clustering identified three distinct expression patterns of SETBP1 targets, with functional enrichment revealing gene sets related to transcriptional regulation, DNA binding, and mitochondrial function. TF activity analysis revealed tissue-specific activity of SETBP1 and its target transcription factors, underscoring tissue context-driven regulation.

citation: SETBP1 is dispensable for normal and malignant hematopoiesis (PMID: 37464069)
summary: Using a newly generated murine model (Vav1-iCre;Setbp1fl/fl), SETBP1 depletion in normal hematopoiesis minimally altered self-renewal, differentiation, or reconstitution in vivo, and did not profoundly alter transcription or chromatin accessibility. Despite expression in long-term hematopoietic stem cells, SETBP1 was found dispensable for AML development or maintenance. These results suggest that a physiologically nonessential gene can act as an oncogene when protein degradation machinery is damaged.

citation: SETBP1 variants outside the degron disrupt DNA-binding, transcription and neuronal differentiation capacity to cause a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 41073373)
summary: Missense variants in SETBP1 outside the degron region cause a clinically variable developmental syndrome through loss-of-function mechanisms impairing ubiquitination, DNA-binding, transcription, and neuronal differentiation capacity and morphologies. Cellular assays and transcriptomics in a cohort of 18 individuals showed these effects are independent of protein abundance, distinguishing them from SGS and SETBP1 haploinsufficiency. This provides evidence that SETBP1 plays a direct role in neuronal differentiation.

citation: SET-binding protein 1 (SETBP1) suppresses cell proliferation in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer (PMID: 39979691)
sample_size: 56 BC tissue samples; 11 mammary cell lines
summary: SETBP1 knockdown in ER-positive breast cancer cells promoted proliferation, inhibited PP2A activity, and increased phosphorylation of MAPK, suggesting SETBP1 acts as a tumor suppressor in this context. Pathway analyses revealed an inverse relationship between decreased SETBP1 expression and E2F, MYC, and G2M checkpoint target gene expression. Low SETBP1 expression was associated with high promoter methylation and DNA copy number deletion, and was an independent prognostic factor for poor recurrence-free survival.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic and functional comparison of identical germline and somatic SETBP1 mutations (R. Acuna-Hidalgo et al.)
summary: Overexpression experiments confirmed that mutations in the SETBP1 hotspot degron destroy a protein degradation signal, leading to increased SETBP1 protein accumulation, with different mutations having varying effects on stability. Saturation genome editing and functional studies showed that mutations more prevalent in leukemia are functionally stronger (more disruptive to the degron) than those causing Schinzel-Giedion syndrome. SGS patients with functionally stronger germline mutations showed increased cell proliferation in vitro, increased malignancy incidence, and decreased survival.

Resequencing of candidate genes in 4,716 additional cases pinpointed SETBP1 among 10 genes enriched for putative loss-of-function variants. This established SETBP1 haploinsufficiency as a cause of a new clinical subtype of pediatric neurodevelopmental disease.

citation: SETBP1-R54P mutation promotes malignant transformation of cadmium-induced 16HBE cells by down-regulating circ_0007095 expression (PMID: 40152245)

This study demonstrates an interaction between SETBP1 genetic variation and epigenetic/epitranscriptomic regulation in environmental chemical carcinogenesis.

Loss of Satb2 in adult mice leads to stable conversion of colonic stem cells into small intestine ileal-like stem cells, while SATB2 confers colonic properties on the mouse ileum. SATB2 regulates colonic identity by modulating enhancer binding of intestinal transcription factors CDX2 and HNF4A.

citation: USP10 promotes glioma stem cell maintenance and glioblastoma growth by antagonizing DTX3L-mediated SATB2 ubiquitination (PMID: 41507172)

Knockdown of USP10 or overexpression of DTX3L markedly downregulates SATB2, inhibiting glioma stem cell self-renewal and GBM growth, which can be rescued by SATB2 overexpression. Pharmacological inhibition of USP10 by Wu-5 effectively suppresses tumor growth.

Satb2 mRNA translation requires eIF4A1 helicase activity towards its 5'-untranslated region, demonstrating post-transcriptional regulation of SATB2. This places SATB2 as a key determinant of cortical neuron identity regulated by proteostasis mechanisms.

ChIP and luciferase reporter assays demonstrated direct suppression of EphA7 expression by Satb2. Overexpression of EphA7 in late-born cortical neurons phenocopied Satb2 knockdown (soma clumping and impaired self-avoidance), and reducing EphA7 rescued Satb2 knockdown phenotypes.

This function was shown to be conserved, as GA also protected lung epithelial cells and mice during P. aeruginosa infection via the homeodomain transcription factor SATB2. citation: Cognitive and Synaptic Impairment Induced by Deficiency of Autism Risk Gene Smarcc2 and its Rescue by Histone Deacetylase Inhibition (PMID: 40492195)
summary: SMARCC2 was significantly diminished in iPSC-derived neurons from idiopathic ASD patients. Smarcc2 deficiency in mouse prefrontal cortex led to impaired working memory, downregulation of synaptic transmission genes, and impaired GABAergic and glutamatergic synaptic currents. Treatment with the HDAC inhibitor romidepsin restored histone acetylation, working memory, and synaptic gene expression in Smarcc2-deficient mice.

citation: SMARCC2 silencing suppresses oncogenic activation through modulation of chromatin accessibility in breast cancer (PMID: 38852505)
summary: SMARCC2 silencing in breast cancer cells suppressed tumorigenesis and reduced cancer stem cell features, revealing a pro-tumorigenic function for SMARCC2 in breast cancer that contrasts with other SWI/SNF subunits. Mechanistically, SMARCC2 depletion downregulated the Ras-PI3K signaling pathway by reducing chromatin accessibility at enhancers of key genes such as PIK3CB. These findings were validated using RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP analyses, and xenograft models.

citation: Elucidating the clinical and molecular spectrum of SMARCC2-associated NDD in a cohort of 65 affected individuals (PMID: 37551667)
summary: Missense variants in SMARCC2 were examined using 3D protein modeling, co-immunoprecipitation, and proximity-ligation assays, revealing decreased protein expression for N-terminal missense variants similar to likely gene-disrupting variants. Non-truncating variants clustered in functional domains and were mostly de novo, associated with severe developmental delay, while LGD variants were predominantly inherited and associated with milder phenotypes. These findings suggest distinct pathomechanisms for different variant classes affecting BAF complex subunit interactions.

citation: Nuclear RIPK1 promotes chromatin remodeling to mediate inflammatory response (PMID: 35661830)
summary: Activated nuclear RIPK1 mediates phosphorylation of SMARCC2, a key component of the BAF complex, to promote chromatin remodeling and transcription of specific proinflammatory genes. The RIPK1/BAF complex is recruited by specific transcription factors to active enhancers and promoters marked by H3K4me1 and H3K27ac upon RIPK1 activation. Increased nuclear RIPK1 activation and RIPK1/BAF-mediated chromatin-remodeling activity were found in cells expressing non-cleavable RIPK1 and in ALS pathological samples.

citation: FBXO28 promotes proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells through regulation of SMARCC2 ubiquitination (PMID: 37348029)
summary: FBXO28 was identified as an E3 ligase that targets SMARCC2 for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation in pancreatic cancer. Upregulation of SMARCC2 reversed the pro-tumorigenic effects of FBXO28 overexpression on proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells. FBXO28 expression was negatively correlated with SMARCC2 levels and with patient survival prognosis.

citation: SMARCC2 mediates the regulation of DKK1 by the transcription factor EGR1 through chromatin remodeling to reduce the proliferative capacity of glioblastoma (PMID: 36418306)
summary: SMARCC2 acts as a tumor suppressor in glioblastoma by negatively regulating transcription of the oncogene DKK1 through chromatin remodeling, closing the DKK1 promoter region bound by transcription factor EGR1. SMARCC2 knockout promoted glioblastoma cell proliferation while overexpression inhibited it, and in vivo overexpression significantly reduced intracranial glioma size in nude mice. The SWIRM domain of SMARCC2 was found to play a more important role than the SANT domain in its chromatin remodeling function.

citation: Expanding the Spectrum of BAF-Related Disorders: De Novo Variants in SMARCC2 Cause a Syndrome with Intellectual Disability and Developmental Delay (PMID: 30580808)
summary: Transcriptomic analysis of fibroblasts from individuals with SMARCC2 variants identified differentially expressed genes with roles in neuronal development and function, including H19, SCRG1, RELN, and CACNB4. SMARCC2 (BAF170) is described as an invariable core subunit of the BAF complex crucial for embryogenesis and corticogenesis. Fifteen individuals with heterozygous SMARCC2 variants presented with neurodevelopmental delay, with more severe phenotypes in those harboring variants in the SANT and SWIRM DNA-interacting domains.

citation: The functional landscape of the human phosphoproteome (PMID: 31819260)
summary: Machine learning analysis of 119,809 human phosphosites identified regulatory phosphosites in SMARCC2 that were experimentally validated to play a role in neuronal differentiation. SMARCC2 is identified as a member of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex with functionally important phosphorylation sites. This study integrated 59 features of proteomic, structural, regulatory, and evolutionary relevance to prioritize functional phosphosites.

citation: Identification of selective SWI/SNF dependencies in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer (PMID: 39905188)
summary: A systematic CRISPR epigenetic library screen identified SMARCC2 as selectively essential in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer models. Chromatin occupancy of SMARCC2 and BRG1 was expanded in enzalutamide resistance at regions overlapping with CRPC-associated transcription factors accessible in clinical samples. These findings reveal a regulatory role for SMARCC2 in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer and support targeting the SWI/SNF complex in late-stage disease.

citation: ASHG 2014 - The discovery of integrated gene networks for autism (O. Penn et al.)
sample_size: 1116 ASD/ID patients; 2661 in full SSC analysis
summary: SMARCC2 was identified as part of a significant gene module (p<0.005) enriched for de novo mutations in ASD and ID patients, associated with the SWI/SNF and NCOR complexes and showing highest expression early during embryonic development. SMARCC2 was also found in an overlapping module for schizophrenia, with mutations observed in both ASD/ID and schizophrenia cohorts. The module containing SMARCC2 was associated with Wnt and Notch signaling pathways.

citation: SOX11 regulates SWI/SNF complex components as member of the adrenergic neuroblastoma core regulatory circuitry. (PMID: 36882421)
summary: SOX11 is identified as a dependency transcription factor in adrenergic neuroblastoma, regulated by adrenergic-specific super-enhancers and part of the core regulatory circuitry (CRC). SOX11 directly regulates 10 SWI/SNF core components including SMARCC1, SMARCA4/BRG1, and ARID1A, as well as HDAC2, CBX2, KDM1A/LSD1, and c-MYB, positioning it as an epigenetic master regulator. citation: Lineage specific transcription factor waves reprogram neuroblastoma from self-renewal to differentiation. (PMID: 38653778)

CRISPR-Cas9 and siRNA knockdown verified SOX11 dependency both in vitro and in vivo. Silencing the SOX11 super-enhancer using dCAS9-KRAB decreased SOX11 mRNA and inhibited neuroblastoma cell growth.

citation: The SOX11:SMARCA4 complex is a driver of oncogenic transcriptional programs in mantle cell lymphoma. (PMID: 40739087)
summary: SOX11 physically interacts with SMARCA4, the catalytic subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex, as validated by co-immunoprecipitation and proteomic strategies. SOX11 and SMARCA4 share binding sites at open chromatin and active promoters, co-regulating key oncogenic pathways including BCR, NIK, and BCL2 signaling in MCL. SMARCA4 expression is directly regulated by SOX11, and PROTAC-mediated SMARCA4 degradation reduced SOX11 binding and induced apoptosis in SOX11-positive MCL cells.

citation: SOX11 is a novel binding partner and endogenous inhibitor of SAMHD1 ara-CTPase activity in mantle cell lymphoma. (PMID: 38237141)
summary: SOX11 was identified as a novel direct binding partner of SAMHD1 via co-immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry in MCL cell lines, validated by proximity ligation assay. In vitro, SAMHD1 bound to the HMG box of SOX11 with low-micromolar affinity, and SOX11-SAMHD1 binding reduced SAMHD1 tetramerization. Functionally, SOX11 expression inhibited SAMHD1 ara-CTPase activity in a dose-dependent manner, resulting in cytarabine sensitization in cell lines and a SOX11-inducible mouse model of MCL.

citation: SOX11, CD70, and Treg cells configure the tumor-immune microenvironment of aggressive mantle cell lymphoma. (PMID: 34189576)
sample_size: 730 immune-related genes analyzed; primary nodal MCL cases
summary: SOX11 directly targets CD70, whose overexpression is induced in SOX11+ MCL tumor cells by CD40L stimulation in vitro. SOX11+ MCL showed significantly lower T-cell intratumoral infiltration and reduced MHCI/II-like and T-cell costimulation transcripts compared to SOX11- cases. CD70 overexpression driven by SOX11 was associated with increased Treg cell infiltration and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment promoting MCL progression.

citation: Human fetal cerebellar cell atlas informs medulloblastoma origin and oncogenesis. (PMID: 36450980)
summary: SOX11 was identified as a transcriptional determinant in transitional cerebellar progenitor populations connecting neural stem cells to neuronal lineages in developing fetal cerebella. SOX11 expression in these progenitors is correlated with clinical prognosis in group 3 medulloblastomas. Genomic and Hi-C profiling identified de novo long-range chromatin loops juxtaposing SOX11-targeted super-enhancers to cis-regulatory elements of MYC, and targeting SOX11 inhibited MYC expression and group 3 MB growth.

citation: Transcriptional dynamics orchestrating the development and integration of neurons born in the adult hippocampus. (PMID: 39028813)
summary: SOX11 (along with SOX4) is identified as a SoxC transcription factor whose activity is shut down during the transition from immature to mature adult-born granule cells in the hippocampus. Overexpression of SOX11 in adult-born granule cells caused them to remain immature, demonstrating that downregulation of SOX11 is required for proper neuronal maturation. This was shown using single-nuclei RNA sequencing combined with functional overexpression experiments.

citation: SOX11 as a potential prognostic biomarker in hepatocellular carcinoma linked to immune infiltration and ferroptosis. (PMID: 39246708)
sample_size: TCGA-LIHC dataset; HepG2 and HuH7 cell lines

Knockdown of SOX11 in HepG2 and HuH7 HCC cell lines resulted in reduced proliferation and migration. SOX11 expression showed significant associations with immune infiltration, ferroptosis-associated genes, and immune checkpoint genes in HCC tissue.

citation: Temporal controls over inter-areal cortical projection neuron fate diversity. (PMID: 34754107)
summary: SOX11 is identified as a temporally differentially expressed transcription factor in motor cortex-projecting versus secondary somatosensory cortex-projecting inter-areal cortical projection neurons (ICPN) in the mouse neocortex. Postnatal manipulation of SOX11 expression in primary somatosensory cortex impaired sensorimotor connectivity and disrupted selective exploratory behaviours in mice. These findings reveal that dynamic differences in SOX11 expression levels contribute to intra-type diversity in cortical neuron circuit connectivity.

summary: Altered TAOK1 expression levels in the embryonic mouse brain affect neural migration in vivo and neuronal maturation in vitro. A cohort of 23 individuals with mostly de novo TAOK1 variants showed a neurodevelopmental disorder comprising facial features, developmental delay/intellectual disability, muscular hypotonia, and feeding difficulties. Both truncating and missense variants were identified, with missense variants showing loss-of-function or dominant-negative effects.

citation: Neurodevelopmental disorder-associated mutations in TAOK1 reveal its function as a plasma membrane remodeling kinase (PMID: 36595571)
summary: TAOK1 is abundant in neurons in the mammalian brain and remodels the neuronal plasma membrane through direct association with phosphoinositides. Four NDD-associated TAOK1 mutations were catalytically inactive and aberrantly trapped in a membrane-bound state, inducing abnormal membrane protrusions and abnormal dendritic arbor growth in cultured mouse hippocampal neurons. Autophosphorylation of threonine-440 and threonine-443 in a triple-helical coiled-coil region blocks plasma membrane association of TAOK1.

citation: Ste20-Like Kinase TAOK1 Positively Regulates Antiviral Responses by Controlling the TBK1-IRF3 Signaling Axis (PMID: 36649698)
summary: TAOK1 positively regulates virus-induced type I interferon production by promoting TBK1-IRF3 complex formation in a kinase activity-dependent manner. TAOK1 is constitutively associated with TBK1 independently of MAVS, and viral infection induces TAOK1 to bind dynein instead of MAP4, trafficking TBK1 along microtubules to the perinuclear region to bind IRF3. TAOK1 deficiency decreased nucleic acid-mediated type I IFN production and increased susceptibility to virus infection.

citation: TAOK1 negatively regulates IL-17-mediated signaling and inflammation (PMID: 29400705)
summary: TAOK1 functions as a negative regulator of IL-17-mediated signal transduction by interacting with IL-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) independent of its kinase activity, dose-dependently preventing formation of the IL-17R-Act1 complex. TAOK1 knockdown promoted IL-17-induced cytokine/chemokine expression and activation of MAPK and NF-κB. TAOK1 deficiency exacerbated colitis in a TNBS-induced inflammatory bowel disease model, and TAOK1 expression was decreased in colons of ulcerative colitis patients.

citation: TAOK1 promotes filament formation in HR repair through phosphorylating USP7 (PMID: 40106350)
summary: TAOK1 plays a pivotal role in the DNA damage response by phosphorylating USP7, thereby promoting its enzymatic activity and preventing ubiquitylation and degradation of RAD51, a crucial protein in homologous recombination (HR) repair filament formation. Genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition of TAOK1 impaired USP7 function, leading to RAD51 degradation, disruption of HR repair, and increased tumor cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition. This identifies TAOK1 as a critical regulator of the HR repair pathway and a potential target to overcome PARP inhibitor resistance.

citation: Thousand and one amino acid protein kinase 1 suppression improves doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by preventing cardiomyocyte death and dysfunction (PMID: 39964965)
summary: A kinome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) identified TAOK1 as a regulator of doxorubicin-induced cardiomyocyte death. TAOK1 suppression improved DOX-induced cardiomyocyte death, sarcomere disarray, contractile dysfunction, DNA damage, and mitochondrial dysfunction via attenuation of p38 MAPK activation. AAV-mediated TAOK1 silencing in mice attenuated DOX-induced myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis, and cardiomyocyte atrophy, improving cardiac function.

citation: Silencing of STE20-type kinase TAOK1 confers protection against hepatocellular lipotoxicity through metabolic rewiring (PMID: 36930872)
summary: TAOK1 mRNA expression in human liver biopsies positively correlated with key hallmarks of NAFLD including hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and ballooning in a cohort of 62 participants. TAOK1 protein fully colocalized with intracellular lipid droplets in human and mouse hepatocytes. TAOK1 silencing alleviated lipotoxicity by accelerating lipid catabolism, suppressing lipid anabolism, and mitigating oxidative/ER stress, while TAOK1 knockdown inhibited ERK and JNK activation and repressed acetyl-CoA carboxylase abundance.

citation: A global phosphosite-correlated network map of Thousand And One Kinase 1 (TAOK1) (PMID: 38479581)
summary: Analysis of 709 qualitative and 210 quantitative differential cellular phosphoproteome datasets identified Ser421, Ser9, Ser965, and Ser445 as the predominant TAOK1 phosphosites, representing TAOK1 in ~75% of datasets. TAOK1 is described as a core member of the Hippo signaling pathway and is linked to microtubule dynamics, checkpoint signaling, and DNA damage response. pSer9 is proposed as an autophosphorylation and kinase activity-associated site, while pSer421 is proposed as a regulatory phosphosite involved in genome integrity maintenance.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Novel de novo TAOK1 variants associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype, macrocephaly, and joint hypermobility (H.M. McLaughlin et al.)
summary: Six individuals with novel de novo heterozygous TAOK1 variants were identified from 9,302 exome cases with neurodevelopmental phenotypes, with a seventh identified through GeneMatcher. Variant types included missense, nonsense, frameshift, and splice site variants, suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance. Clinical features included intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, language and motor delays, hypotonia, macrocephaly, and joint hypermobility, representing the first report of de novo TAOK1 variants causing human disease.

citation: A Genome- and Phenome-Wide Association Study to Identify Genetic Variants Influencing Platelet Count and Volume and their Pleiotropic Effects - ASHG 2012 (K. Shameer et al.)
summary: A GWAS in 13,582 participants of European ancestry identified TAOK1 among genes in chromosomal regions associated with platelet count (PLT) and mean platelet volume (MPV). PheWAS analysis revealed pleiotropic effects of variants in these regions associated with autoimmune diseases, hematologic disorders, hypothyroidism, and myocardial infarction.

citation: SHANK2 is a frequently amplified oncogene with evolutionarily conserved roles in regulating Hippo signaling. (PMID: 32661924)
summary: SHANK2 (homolog of Drosophila Prosap) was identified in a genome-wide Drosophila screen as a novel regulator of the Hippo pathway. In human cell lines, SHANK2 overexpression deregulates Hippo signaling through competitive binding for a LATS1 activator, promoting cellular transformation and tumor formation in vivo. Depletion of SHANK2 in cancer cell lines with deregulated Hippo pathway restores Hippo signaling and halts proliferation.

citation: Inhibitory regulation of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator anion-transporting activities by Shank2. (PMID: 14679199)
summary: Shank2 directly interacts with CFTR via its PDZ domain, as demonstrated by yeast two-hybrid assays and co-immunoprecipitation in mammalian cells. Expression of Shank2 suppressed cAMP-induced phosphorylation and activation of CFTR, while antisense knockdown of Shank2 in colonic T84 cells strongly increased CFTR currents. This indicates Shank2 negatively regulates CFTR-mediated ion transport in epithelial cells.

citation: SHANK2 mutations impair apoptosis, proliferation and neurite outgrowth during early neuronal differentiation in SH-SY5Y cells. (PMID: 33483523)
sample_size: SH-SY5Y cell lines (mono- and bi-allelic mutants)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated frameshift mutations in SHANK2 in SH-SY5Y cells caused impaired neuronal differentiation marker expression, decreased neurite outgrowth, diminished apoptosis, and increased proliferation. Bi-allelic SHANK2 mutations led to increased p-AKT levels, implicating downstream tyrosine kinase receptor signaling, and reduced amyloid precursor protein (APP) expression. These findings reveal SHANK2's role in early neuronal differentiation and its molecular links to AKT signaling and APP.

citation: Autism patient-derived SHANK2B(Y29X) mutation affects the development of ALDH1A1 negative dopamine neuron. (PMID: 38704506)
sample_size: iPSC lines from patient and isogenic controls; knock-in mouse model
summary: A patient-derived SHANK2B(Y29X) point mutation causes an early stop codon and aberrant splicing, specifically impairing SHANK2B isoform expression. iPSCs carrying this mutation fail to differentiate into functional dopamine neurons, an effect rescued by genetic correction. Knock-in mice with the same mutation exhibit autistic-like behavior, decreased ALDH1A1-negative dopamine neurons, and reduced dopamine release in the ventral tegmental area.

citation: SHANK2 establishes auditory hair bundle architecture essential for mammalian hearing. (PMID: 40627398)
summary: SHANK2 localizes to the medial apical surface of developing cochlear hair cells and is regulated by the small GTPase RAP1, independently of known lateral or medial polarity proteins. Hair cell-specific ablation of Shank2 disrupts the characteristic V-shaped outer hair cell bundle geometry and impairs high-frequency amplification without abolishing mechanotransduction. Longitudinal studies show this architectural disruption leads to progressive bundle degeneration and hearing loss.

citation: Shank2 identifies a subset of glycinergic neurons involved in altered nociception in an autism model. (PMID: 37316943)
sample_size: Shank2-/- mouse model; human dorsal spinal cord tissue
summary: High levels of Shank2 expression identify a subpopulation of glycinergic inhibitory interneurons in both murine and human dorsal spinal cord. In Shank2-/- mice, loss of Shank2 causes decreased NMDAR levels at excitatory synapses on these inhibitory interneurons, impairing their activation during nociceptive stimuli. This results in increased activation of nociception projection neurons in laminae I and pain hypersensitivity phenotypes including mechanical allodynia and increased formalin sensitivity.

summary: Shank2 is expressed in bone tissue and its levels increase during osteoblastogenesis. siRNA knockdown of Shank2 inhibits osteoblastogenesis of primary murine calvarial osteoblasts, and Shank2-/- mice show decreased bone mass due to reduced osteoblast differentiation and bone formation. iPSC-derived osteoblasts from a patient with a loss-of-function SHANK2 mutation also showed significantly reduced osteoblast differentiation potential.

citation: ASHG 2017 - A direct regulatory link between microRNA miR-137 and SHANK2 with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders. (S. Berkel, A. de Sena Cortabitarte, C. Fischer, G.A. Rappold)
sample_size: SH-SY5Y cells; mouse primary hippocampal neurons; RNA-Seq from CommonMind Consortium (schizophrenia vs. controls)
summary: In silico analysis identified a putative miR-137 binding site in the SHANK2 3'-UTR. In SH-SY5Y cells and mouse primary hippocampal neurons, miR-137 overexpression significantly reduced endogenous Shank2 protein levels without affecting mRNA, while miR-137 inhibition increased Shank2 protein, indicating post-transcriptional regulation by translational repression. In the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of schizophrenia patients, nearly 29% of validated miR-137 target genes showed significant expression differences, supporting a miR-137/SHANK2 regulatory axis in schizophrenia.

citation: Brain region and gene dosage-differential transcriptomic changes in Shank2-mutant mice. (PMID: 36311025)
sample_size: Shank2 heterozygous and homozygous mutant mice (adult)
summary: RNA-Seq transcriptomic analysis of prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and striatum in Shank2 heterozygous and homozygous mutant mice revealed distinct region-specific transcriptomic patterns involving synapse, ribosome, mitochondria, spliceosome, and extracellular matrix gene sets. In the prefrontal cortex, heterozygous Shank2 mutation increased synaptic gene expression (reverse-ASD pattern) while homozygous mutation decreased synaptic gene expression (ASD-like pattern), demonstrating gene dosage-dependent effects. The three brain regions also differed in expression of ASD-related and ASD-risk genes.

summary: A genetic association study in 630 RCC patients and controls found that the SHANK2 rs10792565 T allele was significantly associated with increased RCC risk (adjusted OR=1.79, 95% CI=1.32-2.44, p=1.96×10-4, q=0.030). citation: Genome-wide CRISPR activation screening in senescent cells reveals SOX5 as a driver and therapeutic target of rejuvenation (PMID: 37832549)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPRa screen in human mesenchymal precursor cells identified SOX5 as a top hit whose activation antagonizes cellular senescence. SOX5 overexpression remodeled epigenomic landscapes and elevated HMGB2 expression by increasing H3K27ac and H3K4me1 at the HMGB2 enhancer, promoting rejuvenation. Lentiviral gene therapy with SOX5 or HMGB2 rejuvenated cartilage and alleviated osteoarthritis in aged mice.

citation: The SoxD transcription factors--Sox5, Sox6, and Sox13--are key cell fate modulators (PMID: 19647094)
summary: SOX5 is a member of the SoxD group of transcription factors that contains a conserved HMG-box DNA-binding domain and a coiled-coil dimerization domain. SOX5 and SOX6 redundantly enhance chondrogenesis but retard gliogenesis; SOX5 specifically hinders melanogenesis, promotes neural crest generation, and controls the pace of neurogenesis. SoxD proteins can enhance transactivation by SOX9 in chondrocytes but antagonize SOX9 and other SoxE proteins in oligodendrocytes and melanocytes.

citation: Sox5 regulates beta-cell phenotype and is reduced in type 2 diabetes (PMID: 28585545)
summary: SOX5 was identified as a regulator of a co-expressed gene module enriched for islet-selective open chromatin genes that are perturbed in type 2 diabetes. Sox5 knockdown induced gene expression changes similar to those in T2D and diabetic animals, reducing depolarization-evoked Ca2+-influx and β-cell exocytosis. SOX5 overexpression reversed expression perturbations in a mouse T2D model and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in human islets from T2D donors.

citation: SOX5 inhibition overcomes PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA-mutated breast and ovarian cancer (PMID: 40274769)
summary: SOX5 was found significantly upregulated in olaparib-resistant BRCA-mutated breast and ovarian cancer cells and contributed to PARP inhibitor resistance by upregulating DNA repair pathway genes and suppressing DNA double-strand breaks. Mechanistically, SOX5 directly interacted with YAP1 and promoted its nuclear translocation by suppressing the Hippo pathway, leading YAP1/TEAD to upregulate homologous recombination-related genes. SOX5 siRNA combined with olaparib sensitized resistant cells and suppressed xenograft tumor growth in mice via increased γH2AX formation.

citation: SOX5 promotes cell growth and migration through modulating the DNMT1/p21 pathway in bladder cancer (PMID: 35880568)
summary: SOX5 was found to be upregulated in bladder cancer tissues and cell lines, and its inhibition suppressed cell growth and migration while promoting apoptosis. SOX5 exerted its oncogenic function by upregulating DNMT1, which in turn suppressed p21 expression via DNA methylation of the p21 promoter. SOX5 knockdown also inhibited xenograft tumor growth in vivo, establishing the SOX5/DNMT1/p21 axis as a potential therapeutic target in bladder cancer.

citation: Transcriptional control of chondrocyte specification and differentiation (PMID: 27771362)
summary: SOX5 and SOX6 are identified as key chondrogenic transcription factors that decisively assist SOX9, the master chondrogenic regulator, forming the 'chondrogenic SOX trio.' SOX5/6 bind to chondrocyte-specific enhancer elements and cooperate with SOX9 to activate chondrocyte marker genes including Col2a1 and aggrecan. SOX5/6 are described as having complementary and partially redundant functions to SOX9 across sequential steps of chondrocyte lineage commitment and differentiation.

citation: Integrative functional genomic analysis of human brain development and neuropsychiatric risks (PMID: 30545854)
summary: Transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling across human brain regions and cell types throughout prenatal and postnatal development revealed that SOX5 converges with other neuropsychiatric risk genes (MEF2C, SATB2, TCF4, TSHZ3) in a small number of gene coexpression modules and distinct cell types. This convergence provides insights into the genomic basis of neuropsychiatric risks. The study highlights SOX5 as a gene with genetic associations to brain-based traits and neuropsychiatric disorders.

citation: Human T-bet governs the generation of a distinct subset of CD11c(high)CD21(low) B cells (PMID: 35867801)
summary: In a patient with inherited T-bet deficiency, chromatin accessibility analysis revealed that T-bet governs CD21loCD11chi B cell differentiation by controlling chromatin accessibility of lineage-defining genes including SOX5. SOX5 was among the genes with reduced chromatin accessibility in the absence of T-bet, placing it downstream of T-bet in the regulatory network for this distinct human B cell subset. This identifies SOX5 as a T-bet target gene relevant to human B cell identity.

citation: GWAS Meta-Analysis of Suicide Attempt: Identification of 12 Genome-Wide Significant Loci and Implication of Genetic Risks for Specific Health Factors (PMID: 37777856)
summary: A large multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis of suicide attempt (43,871 cases and 915,025 controls) identified 12 genome-wide significant risk loci, one of which implicated SOX5. The SOX5 locus was among mostly intergenic loci identified in multi-ancestry and European ancestry admixture analyses. This finding establishes a genetic association between SOX5 and suicide attempt risk.

citation: ASHG 2013 - ZBTB20-dependent transcription regulation imbalance in autism and intellectual disability (R. Koul et al.)
summary: SOX5 was disrupted by a chromosome translocation t(3;12) in a patient with developmental delay and autistic features, and two SOX5 mutations (one missense, one nonsense) were identified in patients with nonsyndromic intellectual disability. ZBTB20 was found to function as a transcriptional repressor of SOX5 in mouse brain, with ZBTB20 expression negatively correlated with SOX5 and other genes involved in neurogenesis, dendritogenesis, and neuronal circuit formation. The study suggests SOX5 and its regulator ZBTB20 are associated with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability.

citation: Essential Role of Sptan1 in Cochlear Hair Cell Morphology and Function Via Focal Adhesion Signaling. (PMID: 34708331)
summary: Hair cell-specific knockout of Sptan1 in mice caused rapid deafness, abnormal stereocilia and cuticular plate formation, and loss of hair cells from middle and apical cochlear turns during early postnatal stages. Sptan1 deficiency reduced cell spreading and induced abnormal focal adhesion and integrin signaling, identifying SPTAN1 as critical for auditory function via focal adhesion regulation.

citation: Loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 and SPTBN4 cause early-onset hereditary myopathy. (PMID: 40842327)
summary: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 (frameshift, nonsense, splice-site) were identified in 14 families with early childhood-onset distal myopathy, with muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration of the distal lower limb anterior compartment. Muscle biopsy revealed myopathic changes, and nonsense-mediated decay of SPTAN1 mRNA was confirmed in patient muscle tissue, extending the SPTAN1 phenotypic spectrum to include skeletal muscle disease.

citation: A shear stress-responsive pathway in monocytes drives cardiopulmonary bypass-induced inflammation via spectrin/RAF1/store-operated calcium entry. (PMID: 41579376)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in THP-1 monocytic cells identified SPTAN1 and RAF1 as novel effectors of hemodynamic (shear) stress. SPTAN1 and RAF1 were found to activate store-operated calcium entry under cardiopulmonary bypass conditions, leading to elevated IL-8 expression, defining a SPTAN1/RAF1/SOCE pathway in sterile inflammation.

citation: Lactylated SPTAN1 Accelerates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Promoting NOTCH1/HES1 Activation and Immunosuppression. (PMID: 41243220)
summary: HBV infection promotes lactylation of SPTAN1 at K1952 and K1957 (mediated by AARS1, reversed by HDAC1), disrupting cytoplasmic liquid-liquid phase separation and driving nuclear translocation of SPTAN1. In the nucleus, lactylated SPTAN1 interacts with CBFB to activate NOTCH1/HES1 signaling, promoting HCC cell proliferation and PGE2-mediated immunosuppression via COX2/mPGES1.

citation: Reduced migration of MLH1 deficient colon cancer cells depends on SPTAN1. (PMID: 24456667)
summary: siRNA knockdown of MLH1 in HeLa, HEK293, and MLH1-positive HCT116 cells decreased SPTAN1 mRNA levels, indicating co-regulation. Overexpression of SPTAN1 rescued migration in MLH1-deficient cells, while SPTAN1 knockdown reduced mobility in MLH1-proficient cells, demonstrating that SPTAN1 is required for normal cellular motility in colorectal cancer cell lines.

citation: Loss of Function SPTAN1 Variants Result in Ataxia and Intellectual Disability. (PMID: 39988451)
summary: Ectopic expression of SPTAN1 p.(Gln1448Pro) and p.(Asn1839del) variants in zebrafish showed reduced protein abundance and impaired axonal localization of Sptan1. The p.(Gln1448Pro) variant failed to restore voltage-gated sodium channel localization in sptan1-null axons, and supplementation with D-aspartate improved motility in sptan1-null zebrafish, suggesting a therapeutic avenue for α-II spectrin-associated motor dysfunction.

citation: Spectrins: molecular organizers and targets of neurological disorders. (PMID: 36697767)
summary: SPTAN1 is expressed ubiquitously in the mammalian nervous system and encodes αII-spectrin, which varies in subcellular localization and specialization across neuronal subtypes. Pathogenic variants in SPTAN1 cause neurological disorders, and mouse model studies have illuminated its roles in neuronal membrane organization, axon initial segment integrity, and myelination.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Suppression of dominant-negative SPTAN1 allele in patient-derived cell lines via antisense oligonucleotide therapy (C. Wang et al.)
summary: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) designed to induce RNase-mediated cleavage of the pathogenic p.D2303_L2305dup SPTAN1 mRNA allele achieved significant knockdown of mutant SPTAN1 expression in patient-derived iPSCs and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells and neurons, as confirmed by qPCR. This variant causes dominant-negative aggregation of thermolabile α/β spectrin heterodimers in glutamatergic neurons, and ASO-mediated allele suppression is being explored as a therapeutic strategy for DEE5.

citation: TCF4 promotes erythroid development (PMID: 30315825)
summary: Overexpression of TCF4 in umbilical cord blood cells resulted in a twofold increase in erythroid colony forming units (CFU-Es), while knockdown caused a dramatic decrease in erythroid colonies. TCF4 knockdown and overexpression both inhibited megakaryocyte colony formation, but had no impact on granulocyte or macrophage colonies. In MDS patients, TCF4 mRNA expression was lower in hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors, and MEPs compared to healthy controls, correlating with lower hemoglobin levels.

citation: Suppression of TCF4 promotes a ZC3H12A-mediated self-sustaining inflammatory feedback cycle involving IL-17RA/IL-17RE epidermal signaling (PMID: 38470486)
summary: siRNA knockdown of TCF4 in human keratinocytes increased IL17C expression, and IL-17C stimulation decreased TCF4 while increasing NFKBIZ and ZC3H12A in an IL-17RA/RE-dependent manner, creating a proinflammatory feedback loop. In the KC-Tie2 inflammatory dermatitis mouse model, TCF4 protein was decreased in lesional skin concomitant with increases in IL-17C and Zc3h12a, which reversed upon genetic elimination of Il17c, Il17ra, and Il17re. Interference with Tcf4 in KC-Tie2 mouse skin increased Il17c and exacerbated the inflammatory skin phenotype, identifying TCF4 as a negative regulator of IL-17C-driven skin inflammation.

citation: Transcription Factor 4 loss-of-function is associated with deficits in progenitor proliferation and cortical neuron content (PMID: 35501322)
summary: Neural progenitor cells and brain organoids derived from Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome patients with TCF4 mutations showed reduced proliferation, impaired neuronal differentiation, reduced cortical neuron content, and impaired electrical activity. TCF4 loss-of-function led to decreased Wnt signaling and diminished expression of SOX genes, culminating in reduced progenitor proliferation in vitro. These phenotypes were rescued by correction of TCF4 expression or pharmacological modulation of Wnt signaling.

citation: Deciphering novel TCF4-driven mechanisms underlying a common triplet repeat expansion-mediated disease (PMID: 38713708)
sample_size: 134 Exp- FECD cases; large cohort of Exp+ and Exp- FECD patients
summary: Long-read, short-read, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of primary patient-derived corneal endothelial cells revealed global altered splicing and TCF4 isoform ratio skewing specifically in CTG18.1-expanded FECD cases. Differential gene expression and exon usage analyses identified expansion-specific transcriptomic biomarkers, supporting both RNA toxicity and TCF4 isoform-specific dysregulation as pathogenic mechanisms. Exome data from 134 CTG18.1-independent FECD cases identified rare, potentially deleterious TCF4 variants in 7/134 cases, suggesting TCF4 variants independent of the repeat expansion also increase FECD risk.

citation: Transcriptional regulation of daily sleep amount by TCF4-HDAC4-CREB complex in mice (PMID: 39745887)
summary: AAV-mediated expression of TCF4 (and related class I bHLH factors TCF3, TCF12) across mouse brain neurons reduced both REM and non-REM sleep duration. TCF4 requires its bHLH domain to regulate sleep amount, and physically interacts with CREB and HDAC4 via this domain to cooperatively regulate daily sleep. The ability of CREB to regulate sleep duration also requires its binding to TCF4 and HDAC4, placing TCF4 in a transcriptional complex controlling sleep.

citation: TCF4 Promotes Neuroblastoma Proliferation and Inhibits Ferroptosis by Transactivating GPX4 Expression (PMID: 40668527)
summary: TCF4 mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated in neuroblastoma tissues and cell lines. TCF4 knockdown reduced proliferation, elevated ROS accumulation and lipid peroxidation, and altered iron metabolism markers (FTH1, TFR1). ChIP and dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct TCF4 occupancy and transcriptional activation of GPX4 promoter, and GPX4 overexpression rescued the anti-proliferative and pro-ferroptotic effects of TCF4 knockdown.

citation: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm (PMID: 30350260)
summary: TCF4 is described as a master regulator that drives downstream transcriptional programs in blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN), and its activity is dependent on the BET protein BRD4. TCF4 expression is a highly sensitive diagnostic marker for BPDCN, augmenting diagnostic specificity alongside CD4, CD56, CD123, and TCL1. BRD4 inhibition provides a therapeutic vulnerability by disrupting TCF4-driven transcriptional programs in this malignancy.

citation: TCF4, schizophrenia, and Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome (PMID: 20421335)
summary: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identified a SNP in intron 4 of TCF4 associated with schizophrenia. TCF4 encodes a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that interacts with other transcription factors to activate or repress gene expression, and haploinsufficiency causes Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome. The review proposes that TCF4, NRXN1, and CNTNAP2 may participate in a shared biological pathway altered in schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders.

citation: Tcf4 Deficiency causes recurrent seizures in mice (PMID: 40619119)
summary: Mice with heterozygous deletion of Tcf4 in Aldh1l1-expressing cells (astrocytes and other cell types) developed astrogliosis by postnatal day 4, severe recurrent seizures beginning at three months, and shortened lifespans—the first PTHS mouse model to exhibit seizures. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed widespread gene expression changes in excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes, including genes associated with epilepsy. Increased neuronal activity was observed in cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, and hypothalamus, demonstrating a critical role for TCF4 in astrocyte-dependent CNS homeostasis.

citation: ASHG 2015 - Convergence of genes and pathways influencing neurodevelopment following suppression of ASD-associated chromatin modifiers and transcriptional regulators in human neural progenitor cells (ASHG 2015)
summary: RNAi-mediated suppression of TCF4 in iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) revealed strong overlap between genes regulated by TCF4 and those regulated by CHD8, converging on cell adhesion and Wnt/Notch signaling subnetworks enriched for ASD-associated genes. The transcriptional consequences of TCF4 loss-of-function in NPCs were significantly correlated with co-expression modules influencing developmental timing in the brain. These findings indicate that highly penetrant TCF4 loss-of-function mutations associated with Pitt-Hopkins syndrome and ASD converge on shared early neurodevelopmental pathways.

summary: STXBP1 is expressed in both synaptic and cytosolic fractions of the brain, interacting with neuronal cytoskeleton and membrane periodic structures including alpha II Spectrin and ARPC2. citation: Impaired neuronal activity and differential gene expression in STXBP1 encephalopathy patient iPSC-derived GABAergic neurons (PMID: 33961044)
summary: Patient-derived iPSC GABAergic neurons with STXBP1 pathogenic variants showed only ~20% reduction in STXBP1 protein despite 50% reduction in mRNA, and exhibited dysfunctional maturation with reduced spontaneous spikes and bursts by microelectrode array. Gene expression analysis revealed dysregulation of epilepsy-, neurodevelopment-, and neurodegeneration-associated genes (KCNH1, KCNH5, CNN3, RASGRF1, SEMA3A, SIAH3, INPP5F), supporting GABAergic dysfunction as a key contributor to STXBP1 encephalopathy pathogenesis.

citation: ASHG 2023 - α-Synuclein pathology in Drosophila melanogaster is exacerbated by haploinsufficiency of Rop: Connecting STXBP1 encephalopathy with α-synucleinopathies (ASHG 2023)

Trehalose feeding reduced insoluble α-synuclein and restored locomotion, providing the first in vivo model evidence that STXBP1 acts as a molecular chaperone suppressing α-synuclein aggregation.

citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 3136: Humanized STXBP1 animal models as a precision medicine approach to detecting pathogenicity in clinical variants (ASHG 2019)

Known pathogenic variants (R292H, R406H, R388X) installed into the humanized locus showed quantifiable functional defects in chemotaxis and electrophysiology assays, with R388X displaying a dominant-negative phenotype approximately 3-fold more severe than heterozygous full gene knockout.

citation: CASK, APBA1, and STXBP1 collaborate during insulin secretion (PMID: 33159991)
summary: Co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry demonstrated that CASK, APBA1, and STXBP1 form a tripartite complex during insulin secretion in pancreatic cells. CASK enhanced APBA1-STXBP1 interaction and mediated their trafficking from cytoplasm to plasma membrane; high fatty acid stimulation reduced expression of all three proteins and impaired insulin secretion, while CASK overexpression rescued this defect.

citation: Impaired cortico-striatal excitatory transmission triggers epilepsy (PMID: 31015467)
summary: Stxbp1 haplodeficient mice exhibited absence seizures with spike-and-wave discharges initiated by reduced excitatory transmission from the neocortex to striatal fast-spiking interneurons (FSIs). Selective Stxbp1 deficiency in cortico-striatal but not cortico-thalamic neurons reproduced seizures, and pharmacological AMPA receptor potentiation in the striatum suppressed spike-and-wave discharges, identifying impaired cortico-striatal excitatory transmission as a key epileptogenic circuit mechanism.

citation: STXBP1 encephalopathy: Connecting neurodevelopmental disorders with α-synucleinopathies? (PMID: 31221716)
summary: STXBP1 (Munc18-1) controls SNARE complex formation and synaptic vesicle exocytosis, and genetic knockout leads to widespread perinatal neurodegeneration. Recent evidence indicates STXBP1 also controls the self-replicating aggregation of α-synuclein, linking STXBP1 function to synucleinopathies including Parkinson disease. This review proposes that concurrent synucleinopathic mechanisms may further impair neural development in STXBP1 encephalopathy.

citation: Homozygous STXBP1 variant causes encephalopathy and gain-of-function in synaptic transmission (PMID: 31855252)
summary: In Munc18-1 null mouse neurons, the homozygous disease variant L446F caused a 2-fold increase in evoked synaptic transmission with reduced paired-pulse plasticity, representing a gain-of-function in release probability distinct from the loss-of-function seen with heterozygous mutations. Protein stability of L446F was less dramatically affected than previously reported heterozygous mutants, demonstrating that STXBP1 mutations can produce divergent cellular effects while sharing an encephalopathic phenotype.

citation: HSV-1 latency-associated transcript miR-H3 and miR-H4 target STXBP1 and GABBR2 genes (PMID: 37668872)
summary: HSV-1 LAT-encoded miRNAs miR-H3 and miR-H4 were shown by bioinformatic prediction and luciferase assay to target the 3'UTR of STXBP1, reducing its expression. Overexpression of miR-H4, miR-H3, or the full LAT transcript in HEK293T cells decreased STXBP1 mRNA by 0.059-, 0.237-, and 0.84-fold respectively, identifying STXBP1 as a component of the GABAergic pathway targeted during HSV-1 latency.

citation: PQBP1-dependent alternative RNA splicing underlies high calorie diet-induced cognitive impairment (PMID: 40502014)
summary: Network analysis of high-fat diet-induced alternative splicing changes identified CASK and Cacnb1 as core molecules that regulate STXBP1, a causative gene for infantile epilepsy syndrome and essential factor for synaptic vesicle release, through direct protein interaction. citation: SYT1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Narrative Review (PMID: 36291375)
summary: SYT1 encodes synaptotagmin-1, a synaptic vesicle protein that acts as the primary calcium sensor mediating Ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter release during synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Dysfunction or genetic variants in SYT1 cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by severe neurological impairment. The review details SYT1's essential role in synaptic vesicle exocytosis and the molecular mechanisms underlying SYT1-associated neurodevelopmental disorder.

citation: Neurotransmitter release is triggered by a calcium-induced rearrangement in the Synaptotagmin-1/SNARE complex primary interface (PMID: 39374398)
summary: Using mutagenesis and electrophysiological experiments, this study shows that the Syt1 C2B domain binds the SNARE complex through a primary interface with two regions: region II binding to SNAP-25 is crucial for Ca2+-evoked release, while region I and other residues mediate vesicle priming and clamping of spontaneous release. Ca2+ triggering of release requires a rearrangement of the primary interface involving dissociation of region I while region II remains bound. Mutations enhancing region I binding increase priming and clamping but strongly inhibit evoked release, revealing distinct functional subdivisions within the Syt1-SNARE interface.

citation: Synaptotagmin-1 serves as a primary Zn2+ sensor to mediate spontaneous neurotransmitter release under pathological conditions (PMID: 40753258)
summary: In hippocampal neurons, elevation of intracellular Zn2+ concentration increases the frequency of spontaneous neurotransmitter release in a Syt1-dependent manner. In a reconstituted system with neuronal SNAREs and Syt1, Zn2+ markedly enhances liposome fusion efficiency via binding to the interface between tandem C2 domains of Syt1, and increases Syt1's capacity to bind anionic vesicles, augmenting vesicle docking. A Syt1 triple mutant (Syt1_3M) at the tentative Zn2+-binding site abolishes this Zn2+-induced spontaneous release activation, identifying Syt1 as a primary Zn2+ sensor under pathological conditions.

citation: Exocytosis and synaptic vesicle function (PMID: 24692137)
summary: Syt1 is the most studied isoform among 16 synaptotagmin isoforms and mediates Ca2+-triggered synaptic vesicle exocytosis by interacting with target membranes and the SNARE/complexin complex, including synaptobrevin 2, syntaxin 1, and SNAP25. The affinities of Ca2+-dependent interactions between Syt1 and its targets (SNARE complexes and membranes) are well correlated with the efficacies of corresponding exocytotic processes. Different SNARE protein isoforms and membrane lipids regulate the efficacy of Syt1-mediated exocytosis.

citation: Abnormal α-synuclein binds to synaptotagmin 13, impairing extracellular vesicle release in synucleinopathies (PMID: 40551252)
summary: Immunoprecipitation in SH-SY5Y cells confirmed that SYT13 binds to SYT1 and SNARE complexes, and SYT13 regulates extracellular vesicle release in association with SYT1 and SNARE complexes. SYT13 overexpression impaired extracellular vesicle release, and SYT1 protein levels at synapses were elevated in dementia with Lewy bodies and multiple system atrophy cases. These findings implicate SYT1 as a key component of the vesicle release machinery disrupted in synucleinopathies.

citation: PQBP1-dependent alternative RNA splicing underlies high calorie diet-induced cognitive impairment (PMID: 40502014)
summary: High-fat diet (HFD) in mice induces alternative splicing of Syt1, and HFD-induced alternative splicing isoforms of Syt1 impair pre-synapse vesicle release in primary neurons. AAV-mediated restoration of Syt1 rescues synaptic and cognitive dysfunctions in HFD mice, genetically supporting Syt1's role in the PQBP1-presynapse axis. Syt1 was identified as playing a specific role in early HFD (1 week) through betweenness-based network analysis of common alternative splicing changes.

citation: Identifying Key Regulators in Odorant Receptor Trafficking (PMID: 41125435)
summary: Syt1 was identified as a gene co-regulated with Rtp1 during olfactory sensory neuron (OSN) maturation using single-cell transcriptomic data. Syt1 protein was found to localize in OSN cilia in both male and female mice. When co-expressed with an odorant receptor, Syt1 (in combination with Rtp1) promoted cell-surface expression of tested odorant receptors, and a physical interaction between Syt1 and odorant receptor Or1ad1 was demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation, suggesting a novel role for Syt1 in odorant receptor trafficking or stabilization.

citation: Using optogenetics to dissect rod inputs to OFF ganglion cells in the mouse retina (PMID: 37426783)
summary: Genetic elimination of Syt1 from cones abolished cone-driven optogenetic responses in retinal ganglion cells, demonstrating that Syt1 is the essential exocytotic Ca2+ sensor for synaptic release from cone photoreceptors. Eliminating both Syt1 and Syt7 from rods blocked synaptic release from rods, and eliminating Syt1 from both rods and cones abolished all responses to optogenetic stimulation. These in vivo mouse experiments establish Syt1 as a critical mediator of photoreceptor synaptic transmission in the retina.

citation: A Novel Palmitoylation-Related Molecular Signature for Predicting and Therapeutically Targeting Alzheimer's Disease (PMID: 41364313)
sample_size: Multiple GEO datasets (GSE5281, GSE29378, GSE36980, GSE122063, GSE132903, GSE33000, GSE44770)
summary: SYT1 was identified as one of seven key AD-associated palmitoylation-related genes (AD-PRGs) prioritized through PPI networks and three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) from transcriptomic datasets. A diagnostic model including SYT1 showed AUC values of 0.834 in the training set and 0.907/0.865 in two external validation sets. Single-gene GSEA indicated SYT1 associations with synaptic function pathways, and protein docking analyses suggested interactions between SYT1 and Aβ/tau, supporting its involvement in AD pathogenesis through roles in vesicle recycling and neurotransmitter release.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Investigating Immune Functions of neuronal genes burdening Autism Spectrum Disorder: An integrated gene expression and mutation analysis (A. Siddappa Niranjana Murthy et al.)
summary: SYT1 was identified among genes with prominent neuro-immune functions from ASD-associated gene databases (SFARI-db, Denovo-db, Genes4denovo-db) and was found to be differentially expressed in ASD post-mortem brain tissues. SYT1 also carried deleterious variation in in-house whole exome sequencing data from Indian ASD children, providing genetic evidence for its involvement in ASD pathogenesis. This study provides the first genetic evidence linking SYT1's neuroinflammatory role to ASD.
